transparency_log:consistency.rule: boolean-via-score dimensions default-aggregate by Min across attesters (fail-secure).
transparency_log:consistency.primitive_constraint: composition of multiple consistency attestations for the same (log_id, tree_size1, tree_size2) MUST use Min, not Mean - a single credible CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID fails the claim for all consumers by default

transparency_log:consistency.rule: transparency_log:consistency participates in the Policy G freshness idiom, but CC's only documented instance names transparency_log:inclusion, not :consistency - consistency's documented partner is instead the CC 5.3.1.1 witness-cosign anti-equivocation gate (a different consumer).
transparency_log:consistency.primitive_constraint: do not assume :consistency is interchangeable with :inclusion in consumer composition recipes

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.rule: transparency_log:cosigned:* is witness-reserved: attesting_key_id.identity_type SET must contain witness (set-membership); rejected at admission (CCS), re-checked at consumption (CCC), forbidden at production (CCP).
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.quote: transparency_log:cosigned:* is reserved: emitter rule is attesting_key_id MUST match a federation_keys row with identity_type=witness
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.primitive_constraint: emitter reservation - non-witness attesting_key_id REJECTED at admission, not merely advisory

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.rule: A cosign is admissible only carrying a consistency proof, cryptographically verified by the Registry against the (tree_size, root) it itself recorded for that witness (exempt on that witness's genesis cosign); missing proof = MALFORMED_REQUEST, non-reconstructing = CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID.
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.quote: witness_quorum_met is therefore quorum on log consistency, not quorum on a string.
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.primitive_constraint: emit requires a mandatory verified-proof package; admission MUST reject missing/non-verifying proofs - a hard admission gate, not consumer scoring

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.rule: Cosigning MULTIPLE distinct witnesses over the same (log, tree_size, root) toward a quorum is the family's core anti-split-view mechanism - aggregation-by-counting-distinct-attesters is REQUIRED here, the structural opposite of testimonial's aggregate-forbidden.
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.primitive_constraint: aggregate REQUIRED (quorum-count-distinct-witnesses via count_valid_witnesses/witness_quorum_met); only blending distinct witnesses into one scalar magnitude is the wrong kind

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.rule: A cosignature's own timestamp must fall within +-5 min of the STH's published signed_at (family-specific specialization of the general CC 2.6.7 freshness bound, keyed to the cosigned artifact's own timestamp).
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.quote: cosignatures with signed_at farther than 5 minutes from the STH's published signed_at MUST be rejected.
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.primitive_constraint: temporal admission gate keyed to the STH's recorded signed_at, not merely producer/consumer clock agreement

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.rule: Every federation-tier admission MUST verify BOTH the Ed25519 and the ML-DSA-65 (bound-payload) halves; a classical-only cosignature MUST be rejected outright, no opportunistic-acceptance window.
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.quote: There is no require_hybrid: false posture.
transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.primitive_constraint: cosignature field hybrid-mandatory at admission; no require_hybrid:false posture exists

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: inclusion (and consistency) carry NO identity_type emitter gate; only cosigned:* is witness-reserved.
transparency_log:inclusion.quote: transparency_log:cosigned:* is reserved: emitter rule is attesting_key_id MUST match a federation_keys row with identity_type=witness
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: admission MUST NOT require witness in identity_type for inclusion/consistency; that gate applies solely to cosigned:*

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: Inclusion is constituted by an independent party actually retrieving+recomputing the proof, not self-announcement - the standalone transparency:{kind} prefix was rejected for smuggling self-declared disclosure.
transparency_log:inclusion.quote: Disclosure is constituted by reception, not announcement.
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: emitter must have performed real retrieval+recomputation; self-published instances independence-downweighted, never a bare self-report substitute for the rejected prefix

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: boolean-via-score => the envelope score field is +-1 only; no partial/graduated value and no separate superset field needed.
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: score MUST be exactly +1.0 or -1.0; a bespoke verification_score 0..1 field duplicates/risks diverging from the typed envelope field - collapse into score

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: Not a standalone trust verdict; one leg of the named Policy G idiom (cert_validity + inclusion + L3/L4 ladder rungs).
transparency_log:inclusion.quote: cert_validity:{authority} + transparency_log:inclusion + (attestation:registry_consensus OR attestation:license_validity) ... 'freshness + attested + verified' idiom.
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: consumer-composition function only, never a wire primitive; a bare +1.0 on this dimension alone is not 'verified'

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: The RFC 6962/9162 Merkle/STH construction is a distinct cryptographic domain from the CC 6.1.1 WholenessWitness scheme; proofs/roots from the two MUST NOT be cross-verified or substituted.
transparency_log:inclusion.quote: the two MUST NOT be cross-verified.
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: audit_path/root checked only against a CC 5.3.1-domain STH, never a wholeness_witness:/member_commitment root, and vice versa

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: New transparency-log integrations MUST use RFC 9162 (CT-bis); 6962 continues only for already-deployed instances.
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: the family description's 'per RFC 6962' is the legacy-interop baseline, not the forward mandate - net-new log_id-producing instances SHOULD target 9162

transparency_log:inclusion.rule: An inclusion proof authenticates presence-in-log; it validates, it never adjudicates the substantive correctness/authorization of what was logged.
transparency_log:inclusion.primitive_constraint: MUST NOT be treated as sole evidence of the certified event's validity/authorization; composes with, never substitutes for, the substantive attestation it anchors (references_attestation_id)

transport:{kind}.rule: Reserved system:* self-report: attesting_key_id.identity_type superset {substrate_edge} (set-membership), steward-triple cross-attested; non-substrate emission is a category error MUST-rejected at admission, never accept-and-downweight.
transport:{kind}.primitive_constraint: emit_authority restricted to a substrate_edge-rooted key; admission MUST reject non-substrate emitters

transport:{kind}.rule: Three-party enforcement triangle: CCS admission-reject, every CCC independent re-check (trust does not propagate), CCP must-not-emit without satisfying the rule.
transport:{kind}.primitive_constraint: admission-reject + mandatory independent consumer re-verification, never trust-propagated

transport:{kind}.rule: {kind} is drawn from the transport-medium vocabulary (Reticulum link types/TransportId), a namespace fully DISJOINT from the 14-member replication-wire EnvelopeKind enum; a leaf validator MUST validate against the transport-medium vocabulary, never EnvelopeKind.
transport:{kind}.primitive_constraint: dimension-leaf validator scoped to transport-medium identifiers, disjoint from EnvelopeKind validation used by the replication layer

transport:{kind}.rule: Rides the single CEG scores workhorse shape; no bespoke per-envelope delivery-trace schema (envelope_hash/route_path/hop_count/delivery_status/retry_count as first-class typed fields).
transport:{kind}.primitive_constraint: no bespoke attestation_envelope shape; per-message hop/route/latency detail belongs in context (free-form) or evidence_refs, never new typed top-level fields

transport:{kind}.rule: Default signed-polarity composition is Mean(score x confidence) per (dimension, attested_key_id) - but since only the reporting substrate_edge instance is ever authorized to emit about its own attested_key_id, this degenerates to temporal composition (most-recent non-superseded self-report), never a cross-node mean of the same fact.
transport:{kind}.cc_ref: CC 4.4.2 (interpretive extension of the single-authorized-emitter structure - flagged as inference)
transport:{kind}.primitive_constraint: composer MUST NOT average DIFFERENT reporting nodes' self-reports as same-subject evidence; cross-node comparison is a distinct consumer-policy operation, not CC 4.4.2 same-subject aggregation

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: Signed-polarity aggregation MUST be Mean(score x confidence) per (dimension, attested_key_id) - never sum/max/min; implemented in compose_policy Signed branch + persist compose_verdict.
truth_grounding:{subject}.quote: signed | Mean of score x confidence across attesters

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: A witness_diversity gate + diversity discount MUST apply to the truth_grounding MEAN ITSELF (not only the vote->weighted_aggregate finality plane); n_eff is annotation only and MUST NEVER be used as an aggregation weight.
truth_grounding:{subject}.cc_ref: FSD-005 sec.7 (RT-C4/E v0.2 fix), grounded in CC 3.1.9.3 + CC 6.1.2.1.2
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: mean-aggregate FORBIDDEN without a diversity discount once witness_diversity data exists; n_eff FORBIDDEN as weight. VERIFIED UNIMPLEMENTED: compose_verdict hardcodes witness_diversity:None; no diversity computation touches the Signed branch - the sock-puppet mean-pulling exposure is live today

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: A cross-attestation on a detection:* detector's verdict MUST ride the distinct truth_grounding:detection:{axis} prefix (never detection:* itself) to avoid shadowing the reserved lenscore_detector emission; this sub-prefix carries NO lenscore_detector requirement.
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: truth_grounding:detection:* emitter requirement = none (open, signed); MUST NOT be admitted/aggregated as a detection:* reserved primary emission - VERIFIED IMPLEMENTED (prefix-ordering in compose_policy)

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: Encyclopedic (knowledge-commons) truth_grounding volume MUST NOT drive NodeCore Credits accrual - decoupled from the Tier-3 governance usage that legitimately does.
truth_grounding:{subject}.cc_ref: FSD-005 sec.11 / REVIEW_LOG:62 (LOW-8), in tension with App.A's own 'drives Credits accrual' line
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: Credits-accrual composer FORBIDDEN from reading encyclopedic-subject truth_grounding rows as fungible with governance-object rows. VERIFIED UNBUILT: no subject-context discriminator exists anywhere - the decoupling has zero enforcement mechanism (unlike the truth_grounding:detection:* prefix which DOES exist)

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: testimonial_witness:* is never sole evidence for slashing; truth_grounding IS an admissible non-testimonial corroborating evidence type for slashing resolution.
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: a slashing evidence-set of ONLY testimonial rows is insufficient; a truth_grounding row is an eligible non-testimonial member - VERIFIED IMPLEMENTED + tested (a truth_grounding:forensics row satisfies the testimonial gate test)

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: recants vs withdraws on a truth_grounding row is NOT self-selectable for reputation-laundering: a debunked-then-withdrawn contradiction must remain distinguishable from a clean voluntary withdraw in downstream reputation composition.
truth_grounding:{subject}.cc_ref: FSD-005 sec.7 (RT-M1/F), grounded in CC 2.4.1 distinction
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: track_record/Credits composer FORBIDDEN from treating contradiction-then-withdraw identically to voluntary withdraw; requires a retained distinguishing signal. VERIFIED UNBUILT: compose_verdict excludes both from heads before open_contradictions - indistinguishable, laundering path open

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: withdraws via the rule-3 canonical-hash proxy requires a verified live delegates_to chain (proof of control), not mere preimage knowledge; PLUS a public-interest carve-out so self-about-subject consent-withdrawal cannot suppress a true adverse public-interest claim.
truth_grounding:{subject}.cc_ref: FSD-005 sec.7, grounded in CC 2.4.1.1 rule 3
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: chain-verification half IS implemented (resolve_withdraws_admission_rule); the public-interest override is ABSENT - VERIFIED UNBUILT (zero public_interest hits)

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: Resolution timeliness/disagreement are federation-health-observable, never silent: hard_case:vote_variance on excess variance; hard_case:resolution_time on exceeding the cell's P75.
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: a resolution composer REQUIRES emitting the corresponding hard_case:* on variance/latency breach

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: Self-attestation (witness_relation:self) about one's own subject is admissible (Ubuntu R4); the consumer/composition layer bears sole responsibility for down-weighting it - admission MUST NOT reject it.
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: admission FORBIDDEN from rejecting witness_relation:self; composition REQUIRED to discount relative to external witnessing

truth_grounding:{subject}.rule: confidence is a REQUIRED base field feeding the mean; the composed verdict must be shown as a qualitative band + n (contributor count / witness_diversity / open-contradiction count), never a bare high-precision percentage.
truth_grounding:{subject}.primitive_constraint: render/serve FORBIDDEN from a bare precision %; MUST project a ConfidenceBand + n. Partially implemented (ConfidenceBand/classify); witness_diversity not yet a real input to 'n'

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: Vote weight is a COMPUTED product of the voter's own Credits and Expertise ledger standing at composition time - never an author-supplied numeric weight in the envelope.
vote:{contribution_id}.quote: vote:{contribution_id} | Signed score on a Contribution (P4). Weight = Credits x expertise multiplier.
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: no self-declared weight field; weight derived downstream from credits:{domain}:{language}:{subject} x expertise:{domain}:{language}. CONFIRMED GAP: zero references to credits/expertise/weighted_aggregate in CIRISServer src/; vote rows fall through polarity_for to plain Signed mean with no multiplier applied

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: vote:* itself computes/holds no aggregate; the rolling tally is the structurally distinct weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id} (P7).
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: aggregate FORBIDDEN on vote:* - one vote is exactly one signed individual score; the tally lives ONLY in weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: The generic (dimension, attested_key_id) grouping cannot produce weighted_aggregate's cross-voter tally because a Contribution has no federation key_id of its own; attested_key_id defaults to the attester (R-C1, confirmed persist engine.rs:2351), collapsing every voter's vote into its own singleton group.
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: weighted_aggregate requires a BESPOKE contribution_id-keyed fold across attesters; the generic composer cannot produce it as-is

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: Slashing is decoupled from disagreement at every decision-hierarchy level; a dissenting/minority vote is never itself grounds for slashing.
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: vote:* (or the mere fact of disagreeing) MUST NEVER be sole/direct input to a slashing composer - slashing fires only on documented P8 allegation types

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: Voting-misconduct detector signals (rogue_vote, coordinated_voting, out_of_distribution_voting) are advisory-only, never sole slashing evidence; WA quorum is the load-bearing gate.
vote:{contribution_id}.quote: ratchet:flag:* cannot be sole evidence for slashing:*.
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: moderation:{rogue_vote,coordinated_voting} + ratchet:flag:{out_of_distribution_voting,coordinated_voting_cluster} feed a ModerationEvent, never a direct slashing input. CONFIRMED GAP: compose_policy implements this screen ONLY for testimonial_witness - no ratchet:flag/detection generic equivalent despite CC 3.1.6

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: Commons Credits (first weight factor) are non-transferable and accrue only per-key via the truth-grounding loop (anti-plutocracy).
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: the Credits factor must never be transferable/delegable/purchasable between keys

vote:{contribution_id}.rule: A Contribution's witness/voter set must clear a diversity bar (N=3 default) before finality; DRAFT elaborates this as gating weighted_aggregate directly.
vote:{contribution_id}.quote: witness_diversity:{contribution_id} | Witness set meets ... bars (P10). N=3 default.
vote:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: witness_diversity:{contribution_id} (boolean-via-score min, already wired generically) names the bar. FLAGGED: nothing in ratified CC OR code makes weighted_aggregate finality conditional on witness_diversity passing - DRAFT open gap, no implementation either way

watchlist:{id}.rule: Per-group, NEVER global: scoped to one community whose authority enables it; a fabric-wide scan-everything configuration is non-conformant (the bulk-surveillance posture CIRIS rejects).
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: enable FORBIDDEN without a bound group_key_id/subject_key_ids=[group]; no fabric-scope or multi-group-wildcard enable

watchlist:{id}.rule: Three-way separation of powers: Fabric holds only the mechanism (matcher hook, auto-fire dispatch, audit chain); Operator holds the licensed hash-DB + NCMEC duty (cannot enable for a group); Authority holds only the opt-in (cannot provision the DB, run the match, or see raw matched bytes).
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: envelope MUST NEVER carry raw hash-DB/pattern/term entries - enable authorizes ONLY toggling a reference watchlist_id already exposed by matcher.databases(); no primitive lets one party do more than its third

watchlist:{id}.rule: CSAM class requires a DUAL scope gate (moderate AND takedown), because enabling Csam authorizes an eventual auto-filed takedown_notice with no human review.
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: class MUST be admission-checked: class==Csam requires moderate+takedown over group_key_id; class==OtherContent requires only moderate (IMPLEMENTED: authority_admits_enable)

watchlist:{id}.rule: No-human-in-the-loop auto-removal is CSAM-ONLY: a Csam match auto-fires takedown_notice{PerceptualHashCsam} (immediate eviction, no counter-notice); every other class MUST route to the named moderator, never auto-evict.
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: auto-eviction/takedown_notice composer FORBIDDEN from firing on a class==OtherContent match; OtherContent routes to is_named_moderator(group, moderate), human-gated, reversible-hide at most

watchlist:{id}.rule: Audit - never silent: enabling emits hard_case:watchlist_enabled:{group} (who + which list); every match emits hard_case:watchlist_match:{group}.
watchlist:{id}.quote: Enablement and matches are on the record, always.
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: enable_watchlist/on_publish-match MUST emit a hard_case:*. GAP: HARD_CASE_WATCHLIST_ENABLED/MATCH declared in watchlist.rs but never referenced/emitted - the audit-never-silent floor is unimplemented

watchlist:{id}.rule: CSAM-disable non-silent floor: disabling a CSAM watchlist MUST itself be audited (the withdraws additionally emits hard_case:watchlist_enabled disable variant); ordinary lists may be freely toggled without it.
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: disable_watchlist MUST branch on class: Csam disable REQUIRES a co-emitted audited hard_case; OtherContent has no such floor. GAP: current disable_watchlist has no class parameter/branch and emits no hard_case regardless

watchlist:{id}.rule: Structural-invisibility limit: detection can never reach cohort_scope self|family content; CEG does not claim to solve private-content CSAM detection and does not mandate client-side scanning.
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: matcher-invocation composer FORBIDDEN over content whose cohort_scope suppresses holds_bytes (self/family); no client-side-scanning primitive may compose onto this family

watchlist:{id}.rule: No new structural primitive - rides scores/config over delegates_to; enforced-admission via chain-walk only, never a self-declared on_behalf_of; absence of a field is never an admit condition.
watchlist:{id}.primitive_constraint: enable/disable MUST compose over attestation_upsert_local + withdraws + delegates_to chain-walk; authority proven ONLY by a live, unrevoked, depth<=5 steward-rooted chain (or the zero-hop as-self case)

weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.rule: weighted_aggregate's finality (basis for a downstream decision: proposal adoption, WA promotion, deferral consensus) is GATED by witness_diversity:{contribution_id}=true (boolean-via-score, N=3 diversity bar). CURRENTLY UNENFORCED: compose_contribution_at carries the two as unrelated sibling fields; build_promotion_attestation takes an untyped aggregate_evidence blob with no witness_diversity param.
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.quote: the rolling tally (P7) of vote:*, finality gated by witness_diversity.
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: weighted_aggregate MUST NOT be sole/ungated input to a promotion/adoption composer; requires a joined witness_diversity(contribution_id)=true check - proposed, unimplemented

weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.rule: vote/weighted_aggregate are scoped to NodeCore governance decisioning; must NOT be repurposed as the confidence-composition mechanism for other subject domains (e.g. encyclopedic/Knowledge-Commons claim confidence, which composes truth_grounding by mean).
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.quote: vote/weighted_aggregate (NodeCore governance) are NOT reused for encyclopedic confidence.
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: cross-domain reuse of the weighted_aggregate composer over non-NodeCore-governance Contribution kinds FORBIDDEN

weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.rule: The cohort sub-leaf may only aggregate per-occurrence Contributions each occurrence independently signed with its own key - it can never manufacture/attribute a Contribution to an occurrence that didn't sign it; selective inclusion must be checked via expected_occurrence_count coverage + P10 diversity on the cohort attestation itself.
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.cc_ref: MISSION Primitive 7 cohort-extension (NodeCore#16); aggregate.rs threat comment
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.quote: The cohort can only AGGREGATE existing signed Contributions from the listed occurrences.
weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: aggregate over the cohort sub-leaf FORBIDDEN from synthesizing a contribution not independently signed by its listed occurrence key; REQUIRES a coverage-ratio check (included/expected) before the cohort attestation is treated as complete-or-justified

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: Witness role is gate-only, never adjudication: witnesses attest only that a Contribution warrants review and evidence is well-formed; adjudication is the WA quorum's task.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.quote: The witness role is not adjudication ... Adjudication is the WA quorum's task.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: witness_diversity attestations FORBIDDEN as sole/direct decision-maker of a Contribution's outcome; never substitutes for or short-circuits WA quorum (P8/P11) - precondition gate only

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: Four-condition structural bar, N=3 default, locality-scaled: jurisdictional span>=2, no shared legal entity pairwise, distinct client implementations, nonzero per-witness Expertise standing; N scales with locality:decision:{scale}.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: meets_bar MUST be a conjunction of four discrete/set-level conditions over an N-sized roster; N REQUIRED to read locality:decision:{scale}, not a hardcoded constant

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: Diversity attributes MUST be independently attested, never self-declared inline (RT-M4).
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.quote: Diversity attributes are attested, not self-declared ... else a ring varies declared attributes to inflate witness_diversity (RT-M4).
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: each roster entry's jurisdiction/org/software_stack/cell_expertise tag FORBIDDEN as a raw self-declared string; REQUIRED to carry a references_attestation_id to an independent verifiable attestation

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: Fail-secure MIN aggregation across independent emitters, never mean; n_eff (storage-mass metric) FORBIDDEN as a substitute weight (finding X4).
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.quote: n_eff is annotation, never the weight.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: multiple verdicts for the same contribution_id MUST compose via MIN, never mean/majority; n_eff never a weight

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: Cell-expertise checked at Expertise-granularity (domain, language), not Credits-granularity (domain, language, subject) - witnesses evaluate substantive merit broader than any single subject.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: cell_expertise axis MUST key off expertise:{domain}:{language} (2-tuple), NOT credits:{domain}:{language}:{subject} (3-tuple) - an easy granularity-mismatch bug

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: P10 reaches beyond flat top-level Contributions: cohort attestations (weighted_aggregate:{contribution_id}:cohort:{agent_template_id}) and Tier-2 (P12-P15) dimensional claims.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: {contribution_id} resolution REQUIRED to also cover compound cohort forms + Tier-2 P12-P15 admission sites; a flat-only implementation misses required call sites

witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.rule: Mandatory-gate scope is an enumerated high-stakes trigger set (ModerationEvents, WA candidacy, policy proposals above a magnitude threshold, ExpertiseAttestations jumping the target past a threshold), not universal.
witness_diversity:{contribution_id}.primitive_constraint: admission-time rejection-on-failure applies ONLY to the enumerated set; other kinds may emit witness_diversity (open) but it is not admission-mandatory for them - the mandatory-vs-optional branch keys off Contribution kind + magnitude, not dimension presence

consent:*.rule: consent:* rides the existing `scores` attestation_type exclusively; no leaf in this family may mint a new attestation_type or envelope field (the 1+4 lockdown holds for the whole family, including consent_record and consent:replication).
consent:*.quote: No new attestation_type. [...] not a new structural primitive (the 1+4 surface is frozen; this rides the existing `scores` attestation_type and adds no envelope field)
consent:*.primitive_constraint: emit-composer FORBIDDEN from minting a new EnvelopeKind/attestation_type for any consent:{kind} leaf; must ride bare `scores` (or the `consent_record` subject_kind as ceremony sugar over the identical admission gate)

consent:*.rule: Multi-subject consent revocation composes by OR-over-per-subject-terminal-state; consumer/substrate policy MUST NOT apply majority-rules or all-subjects-must-agree softening -- any one named subject's admitted withdraws evicts the Contribution for all.
consent:*.quote: Consumer policy MUST treat T as revoked from the perspective of all subjects (no "majority-rules" or "all-subjects-must-agree" softening)
consent:*.primitive_constraint: revocation-resolution composer FORBIDDEN from quorum/aggregate-gating a subject's own withdraws against other named subjects' agreement

consent:*.rule: A subject-side consent:state:revoked (or an admitted withdraws under CC 2.4.1.1 rule 2/3) is federation-tier BY CLASSIFICATION: it may transit local-tier as a momentary staging buffer but its only conformant terminal states are federation-tier-promoted or overdue-flagged -- it must never settle as a durable local row.
consent:*.quote: a subject revocation is never a durable local row. Its only conformant terminal states are promoted [...] or overdue-flagged -- never settled local
consent:*.primitive_constraint: promote-with-full-placement primitive for this dimension MUST drive toward federation-tier placement (hybrid signature) within the 24h SLA or emit hard_case:consent_revocation_promotion_overdue

consent:*.rule: A consent:replication:{version} grant's witness_relation MUST be self -- a G->P grant is required to be G's first-person self-attestation of its own replication intent, which is what forecloses a third party forging a grant in G's name.
consent:*.quote: witness_relation = "self" (REQUIRED -- a G->P grant is G attesting about its own replication intent; pinning self is what forecloses a third party forging a grant in G's name...)
consent:*.primitive_constraint: replication-grant admission composer MUST reject a consent:replication:{version} attestation whose witness_relation != self. ENGINEERING FINDING: no such admission check exists in CIRISPersist today -- grep of src/federation/admission.rs finds zero references to consent:replication or GRANT_DIMENSION; honored only by CIRISServer's producer-side emission code (src/peer.rs), violating the CC 3.4.7 three-actor (CCS/CCC/CCP) enforcement pattern

consent:*.rule: A producer narrowing a live consent:replication grant's attestation_prefixes set MUST supersede with a new grant carrying the narrower set; it MUST NOT silently drop a prefix from a still-live grant.
consent:*.quote: it MUST NOT silently drop a prefix from a still-live grant (a silent narrowing is indistinguishable, to a consumer, from no change -- and the cessation obligation below can only attach to an explicit retract/supersede)
consent:*.primitive_constraint: grant-mutation composer FORBIDDEN from in-place attestation_prefixes narrowing without a supersedes/references_attestation_id chain; no admission check exists that rejects a same-owner replacement grant with a narrower prefix set lacking a supersedes reference

consent:*.rule: Dimensions whose namespace pattern names a subject -- including consent:partnered:{user_key} -- MUST carry that subject in subject_key_ids; this closes the default-leak failure mode where subject-bearing content publishes without wire-level subject authority.
consent:*.quote: Dimensions whose namespace pattern names a subject MUST carry `subject_key_ids` containing that subject. This closes the default-leak failure mode...
consent:*.primitive_constraint: emit-composer for consent:partnered:{user_key} (and any future consent:{...}:{key_id}-shaped leaf) MUST populate subject_key_ids superset {that key_id}

consent:*.rule: Subject-side revocation authority does NOT extend to recants -- only the original attester may recant their own claim; a subject exercising consent authority is confined to withdraws / consent:state:revoked.
consent:*.quote: subject-side authority does NOT extend to `recants` (the falsity-admission primitive) -- only the original attester can `recant` their own claim.
consent:*.primitive_constraint: subject-authority composer is FORBIDDEN from routing consent revocation through recants across this entire family

consent:*.rule: The CC-3.1 machine-readable namespace-registry generator (tools/build_cc_namespace.py, vendored as manifests/namespace_registry.json -> CIRISPersist#425 authority_for()) is scoped BY DESIGN to `### 3.1.N` per-owning-component headings only. consent:* lives entirely under CC 3.3 'Content-ingestion prefixes', a sibling top-level section the generator never walks -- so authority_for("consent:...") falls through to ProducerSteward not because the Constitution is silent, but because the vendoring tool's documented scope boundary excludes CC 3.3 wholesale.
consent:*.cc_ref: part_3_the_namespace.md headings CC 3.1 vs CC 3.3; tools/build_cc_namespace.py lines 9-11, 31-44
consent:*.quote: Section CC 3.1 (`### 3.1.1` ... `### 3.1.10`, minus the 3.1.7 summary) catalogs the prefix families by owning component
consent:*.primitive_constraint: tooling/registry-maintenance defect, not a per-object primitive rule: fixing authority_for() classification requires extending the generator's source-section walk (or adding a supplemental CC-3.3 families table), never writing new constitutional prose

trace:*.rule: Every federation-tier trace row (the 'per-trace / store-and-replicate' bulk path) MUST carry and have verified a valid ML-DSA-65 half in addition to Ed25519 - there is no lighter-weight exemption for trace rows versus operational-authority grants, and the substrate MUST reject (never store-then-quarantine) a federation-tier trace lacking it.
trace:*.quote: A federation-tier trace written to the durable, content-addressed, replicated corpus MUST carry (and a verifier MUST check on ingest) the ML-DSA-65 half exactly as a `key_grant` does; there is no "operational authority vs testimony leaf" exemption.
trace:*.primitive_constraint: trace:* admission at the federation-tier boundary MUST verify BOTH Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65; classical-only admission FORBIDDEN; no local-tier/testimony-leaf carve-out once promoted

trace:*.rule: A Contribution (including a trace) is local-tier-eligible (self-read-only, deferred signature) only while its producer holds SOLE revocation authority; the moment a subject other than the producer holds revocation authority over it, it must be signed/promoted, never left local.
trace:*.quote: A write is local-tier-eligible iff the producer holds sole revocation authority over it.
trace:*.primitive_constraint: trace:* deferred-signature/local-tier backlog eligibility is conditioned on subject_key_ids containing ONLY the producer; naming a second subject forfeits local-tier eligibility per the CC 2.4.1.1 rule-2 consequence

trace:*.rule: The delegated_scope capability that gates who may SERVE trace content (infra:serve) is a server-class-only scope: a node-role delegate may hold infra:* scopes but is cryptographically forbidden from also holding any agency:* scope, and a verifier MUST reject an infra-only key presenting agency:*.
trace:*.quote: `infra:*` | server-class (allowed for a `node`-role delegate) ... MUST NOT receive agency - [CC 1.13.5] "infrastructure must not have agency." ... a verifier MUST reject (treat as non-conformant, never grant) an infra-only key presenting any agency:* scope.
trace:*.primitive_constraint: the trace:* SERVE-gate capability token (infra:serve) may ONLY be conferred on a pure node-role (non-agency) delegate; a verifier MUST reject any grant mixing infra:* with agency:* on the same delegation

trace:*.rule: Absent a reserved-prefix registry entry, namespace emission defaults to open-vocabulary / producer-composed trust - the CC 3.4 posture trace:* currently sits under (no accord_holder-style role gate exists for it).
trace:*.quote: Most of the namespace is open-vocabulary - anyone may emit, and trust is composed downstream. A small number of prefixes are reserved: only specific identity types may emit them.
trace:*.primitive_constraint: trace:* emit-authority defaults to ProducerSteward (open) absent ratification; persist's stricter self-emission-mandatory admission rule is a machine-checked interim ahead of, not yet backed by, a CC reserved_rule

trace:*.rule: A `withdraws` against a Contribution is admitted from any key_id that is a member of that Contribution's subject_key_ids, independent of the original producer.
trace:*.primitive_constraint: any additional subject named on a trace row gains independent revoke authority over it - composes with the CC 5.3.2.4.1 local-tier carve-out above

trace_manifest:*.rule: Reasoning-trace emission is NOT reserved and requires no special identity_type: it rides the ordinary agent-role open-vocabulary surface. A key cohabiting the agent role with any other role still emits trace:* under the plain agent surface.
trace_manifest:*.primitive_constraint: authority class = ProducerSteward, reserved_rule = null (confirmed structurally: authority_for() finds no registry entry for any trace:* dimension and falls through to the bare ProducerSteward default)

trace_manifest:*.rule: CC 3.1.5 catalogues the DMA verdicts, conscience verdicts, and six accord-principle scores as INDIVIDUALLY attestable dimensions, each independently signed and composable. The constitution is silent on what happens when those same verdicts are bundled, in ordered form, inside a single outer envelope's components[] array (the trace:complete:v1 shape).
trace_manifest:*.primitive_constraint: constitution-silent: no rule states whether a dma:*/conscience:* verdict embedded inside a trace's components[] is an independently-attestable CEG row or a CEG-invisible payload copy - meaning any consumer-side composition rule written against the standalone dimensions cannot see embedded copies. Directly touches the CEG-replication audit anti-pattern (trace_events must be CEG objects, never copy/outbox).

trace_manifest:*.rule: An oversize trace (canonical bytes > MAX_ATTESTATION_ENVELOPE_BYTES) ships as a manifest (content_hash + byte_len + component_count) rather than inline; fountain-based content recovery for an oversize trace does not exist yet.
trace_manifest:*.cc_ref: unratified 'CC#38' (persist-tracked interim, not yet a Constitution section)
trace_manifest:*.primitive_constraint: a trace_manifest:v1-shaped row is an INTEGRITY-ONLY commitment, not a content-availability commitment. It MUST NOT be treated as content-equivalent to an inline trace by any consumer needing component-level detail - notably CC 3.1.8.4's detection:correlated_action:{axis} F-3 detector, whose declared data source is 'federation-emitted signed traces': once a trace goes oversize and ships manifest-only, that detector's input silently degrades to a bare existence-hash with zero content, for exactly the highest-value cases.

trace_manifest:*.rule: trace:complete:v1 carries no weight/score value in every mint site found (weight: None in both the live mint and the backfill mint) - unlike every neighboring CC 3.1.5 dimension, which are uniformly 'signed' polarity. A trace attestation is a presence/existence record, not a graded verdict.
trace_manifest:*.cc_ref: no direct CC citation - inferred from the uniform 'signed' polarity column at CC 3.1.5 contrasted against the actual code
trace_manifest:*.primitive_constraint: polarity = n/a; numeric aggregation/averaging of trace:* rows is a category error and must be forbidden. NOTE: currently UNENFORCED - check_trace_dimension_admission never inspects weight, so nothing stops a future caller attaching a numeric weight to a trace:* mint.

trace_summary:*.rule: Reasoning-trace dimensions require no separate reserved identity_type; emission rides the agent role's open-vocabulary surface, and this is unaffected by key/role cohabitation.
trace_summary:*.quote: Reasoning-trace dimensions: no separate reserved `identity_type` required; reasoning-trace emission rides the agent role's open-vocabulary surface. Cohabitation does not change this.
trace_summary:*.primitive_constraint: sender gate = open-vocabulary emission path, NOT a reserved-prefix path; no dedicated identity_type may be required as a precondition to emit trace_summary:*

trace_summary:*.rule: capacity:* (the ONLY primitive trace_summary is known to feed) rejects self-emission - attesting_key_id MUST NOT equal attested_key_id - and this anti-Goodhart floor survives key-role cohabitation.
trace_summary:*.quote: `capacity:*` rejects self-emission: `attesting_key_id` MUST NOT equal `attested_key_id`. ... A folded `{agent, lenscore_detector}` key still MUST NOT score its own `capacity:*`. Role cohabitation does not create a self-attestation backdoor.
trace_summary:*.primitive_constraint: trace_summary MUST NEVER be directly promoted into a capacity:* verdict by the same key that authored it - the feature-extraction step (self-authored, expected) and the scoring/composition step (anti-Goodhart-gated) are two DISTINCT primitives that must never collapse into one.

trace_summary:*.rule: Visibility (cohort_scope), revocability (subject_key_ids), and receipt (delivery_mode) are three independent wire axes - none is inferable from another - and self-consent (attesting_key_id in subject_key_ids) is a named, legitimate shape for an agent attesting about its own content.
trace_summary:*.quote: Visibility | `cohort_scope` ... | Who can SEE the data. Revocability | `subject_key_ids` | ... Who can REVOKE the data. Delivery | `delivery_mode` ... | Who actively RECEIVES the data ... When `attesting_key_id` is in `subject_key_ids`, the Contribution is a self-consent ceremony.
trace_summary:*.primitive_constraint: recipient_see / recipient_revoke / recipient_receive must each be evaluated on their own wire field for trace_summary - a family-specific override on one axis must not be assumed to imply anything about the other two.

trace_summary:*.rule: A node's standing grant to replicate attestations to a named peer is scoped per-prefix by attestation_prefixes with trailing-colon-significant, exact-string-prefix matching - a grant naming one prefix family does not thereby cover a different, textually-non-covering prefix family.
trace_summary:*.quote: `attestation_prefixes` is the [CC 2.6.1] JCS-canonical array of [CC 3.1] namespace-prefix strings G consents to replicate (trailing `:` significant - e.g. `"capacity:"`), sorted ascending + deduplicated, so two implementations ... agree byte-for-byte.
trace_summary:*.primitive_constraint: promotion of trace_summary:* across the local-tier->federation-tier consent boundary requires its OWN attestation_prefixes entry in a live consent:replication:v1 grant - a grant scoped to "trace:" does not authorize replicating trace_summary:*, and vice versa (code-conformant: consent_grammar.rs covers() tests this exact non-coverage).

trust:*.rule: The ONLY constitutionally-ratified trust-root primitive today (cohort_subkind: infrastructure) requires FOUNDER-QUORUM admission with an entrenched consensus_protocol - never a bare unilateral self-declaration. The single-key charter self-loop implemented in trust_root.rs has no analogous external-quorum gate at genesis (only at recovery/rotation).
trust:*.primitive_constraint: charter genesis MUST be externally witnessed (quorum-style), never a unilateral self-loop, if it is to inherit CC 3.2's anti-Sybil legitimacy

trust:*.rule: Cycles on the delegates_to graph, including the trivial A->A case, MUST be detected and the cycle-closing emission rejected by the substrate.
trust:*.quote: Cycles (A -> B -> A) | Substrate MUST detect cycles on the delegates_to graph and reject the cycle-closing emission
trust:*.primitive_constraint: self-referential delegates_to(root->root) is the degenerate 1-hop cycle this rule requires substrates to REJECT - the family's core admission mechanism is in direct, unresolved tension with this already-ratified anti-pattern

trust:*.rule: Standing in the federation is constituted relationally through attestation by others, never through self-declaration; the wire format should resist primitives that let a single key announce its own state without external composition.
trust:*.quote: standing is constituted relationally through attestation by others, not through self-declaration... The wire format should resist primitives that let a single key announce its own state without external composition.
trust:*.primitive_constraint: root-hood (exactly what the charter self-loop asserts) is precisely the single-key self-announced state this clause tells producers not to emit; CIRISConstitution#40 ratification must either add an explicit CC 4.1 carve-out for infra-charter self-loops or require external co-attestation

trust:*.rule: A delegates_to whose target's identity_type is node-only MUST carry only infra:* scopes; a verifier MUST reject an infra-only key presenting any agency:* token.
trust:*.cc_ref: CC 4.4.3.4.3 (lines 741, 748) - note the constitution's own cross-reference to 'CC 1.13.5' is a mis-citation; the rule is stated freestanding at part_3:510 and part_4:741-748
trust:*.primitive_constraint: governs every token in the family's RC3 infra:* vocabulary table; CONFIRMED already enforced at admission (scopes_are_infra_only ~line 5748) - no gap here, cited for completeness

trust:*.rule: Down-chain grants attenuate only (child.scope subset of parent.scope), traversal depth is capped at 5 hops by default, and a withdraws at any link invalidates everything downstream.
trust:*.primitive_constraint: the family's 'attenuation-bound, no amplification, ever' design is this existing CC rule applied with the charter as root - but the depth-cap and cycle-rejection legs are not visibly implemented in trust_root.rs's own walk (which only ever looks one hop) and should be audited against a longer chain

trust:*.rule: A withdraws Contribution is admitted only via one of 4 enumerated authority paths (self-withdraw, subject revocation, proxy delegation, delegated revocation).
trust:*.primitive_constraint: the trust-root family's m-of-n charter-recovery supersession is a novel, not-yet-enumerated 5th revocation authority path; needs its own CC subsection to bind other CEG-conforming consumers

trust:*.rule: delegation_purpose: owner_binding is the ONE single-valued delegates_to sub-relation; every other purpose remains a multi-parent DAG.
trust:*.primitive_constraint: trust(user->root) is explicitly multi-valued by design - it must never be implemented as, or conflated with, delegation_purpose: owner_binding; if formally registered it needs its OWN distinct purpose token (e.g. trust_root), and today's code doesn't check delegation_purpose at all

trust:*.rule: accord:* is reserved to accord_holder-only identity_type, CC 3.4.1.
trust:*.primitive_constraint: confirms the family's ACCORD_LIFECYCLE_DIMENSION already resolves correctly through the existing reserved rule - the gap is entirely on the delegates_to/charter overlay, which the CC 3.1 dimension-registry mechanism structurally cannot express (it only catalogs scores dimensions, not delegation_purpose values or scope-token vocabularies)

ownership:*.rule: A node/agent key is owner-bound by AT MOST ONE responsible steward at any time; owner_of MUST resolve to at most one key and MUST NOT be resolved by picking off a sorted/lexicographic set on cardinality>1 - it is a hard fail-closed error, not a tie-break.
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: owner_of/single-owner resolution FORBIDDEN from using aggregate, majority, or deterministic-pick composition; cardinality != 1 -> fail-closed. IMPLEMENTED: owner_of returns Error::AmbiguousNodeOwner on cardinality>1; check_single_node_owner_admission rejects a second distinct owner AT admission time.

ownership:*.rule: The owner-binding's attesting_key_id MUST equal the claimed owner (self-attestation is the claim of ownership); the FIRST (genesis) binding is additionally set at provisioning, not decided by who reaches the substrate first.
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: sender == claimed-owner REQUIRED (self-emit required, inverse of the registry's existing no-self-emit reserved_rule pattern). IMPLEMENTED: build_owner_binding_envelope/build_signed_owner_binding signs with the responsible user's own LocalSigner.

ownership:*.rule: While a live owner-binding exists, the substrate MUST reject a second, distinct-owner binding at bind time; the incumbent must withdraws/recants first (or lapse). Ownership transfer is explicit, never accretive.
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: delegates_to(delegation_purpose=owner_binding) admission is NOT append/accrete. IMPLEMENTED: check_single_node_owner_admission -> Error::NodeAlreadyOwned, wired into memory/sqlite/postgres put_attestation.

ownership:*.rule: No permanent ownerless lock: a key rendered ownerless by a provably-dead incumbent MUST remain re-claimable via WA/recovery-authority-adjudicated liveness finding; the SAME recovery authority MAY also withdraw a binding found to be a live wrongful seizure.
ownership:*.cc_ref: CC 3.2 (part_3_the_namespace.md:503, citing the CC 4.2.6 restore-path adjudication by analogy)
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: reclaim of a LIVE incumbent's binding requires WA/recovery-authority adjudication, never node self-attestation, never unilateral majority. NOT IMPLEMENTED as a concrete wire path in CIRISPersist v21.4.0: the CC 2.4.1.1 rules 1-4 have no path for a third-party WA to withdraws a LIVE incumbent's owner-binding absent a pre-existing delegation FROM that incumbent (chicken-and-egg for a dead/absent owner); grep finds zero occurrences of seizure/reclaim/provably-dead/ownerless. A genuine, filed-worthy gap.

ownership:*.rule: owner_of is the PURPOSE-FILTERED read (delegation_purpose: owner_binding only); a reader that returns every live delegates_to(user->K) regardless of purpose MUST NOT be used to resolve ownership.
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: ownership resolution MUST purpose-filter on delegation_purpose==owner_binding, never on the generic is_steward_bound predicate. IMPLEMENTED, with a documented historical near-miss: CIRISPersist#378 added recognizing delegation_purpose=='owner_binding' as an ADDITIONAL discriminator after finding the internal-dimension-only gate could be bypassed by the raw emit_attestation_self path - a real instance of exactly the 'carried in extra, invisible to compiler, incomplete primitive shipped' failure class this walk exists to find, since fixed.

ownership:*.rule: A delegates_to whose attested/target key resolves to a node-only identity_type MUST carry ONLY infra:* delegated_scope; agency:* MUST be rejected.
ownership:*.cc_ref: CC 4.4.3.4.3 (part_4_composition_governance.md:741-748); principle referenced as CC 1.13.5 in the constitution's own cross-references, though this checkout's CC 1.13.5 does not contain that text - cross-reference drift
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: delegated_scope on a node-only-target owner/steward binding FORBIDS agency:*. IMPLEMENTED: check_node_agency_admission -> Error::NodeAgencyForbidden, wired into all three backends; CIRISServer's producer-side scopes_are_infra_only gate composes the identical predicate.

ownership:*.rule: delegation_purpose: owner_binding is the ONE delegation_purpose value that is single-valued; act-on-behalf, hierarchy (CC 4.5.13), and authority-source delegations remain multi-parent DAGs.
ownership:*.primitive_constraint: single-owner cardinality gate applies ONLY to delegation_purpose==owner_binding rows. IMPLEMENTED: check_single_node_owner_admission is a no-op for any non-owner-binding delegates_to.

config:*.rule: Config-class content ('memory / config / consent / identity') is normatively cohort_scope:self, DEK-wrapped via the CC 4.4.3.4.1 Policy-L key-grant cascade, and shared identically between a Self's occurrences - not a federation-tier broadcast.
config:*.quote: Both receive the Self DEK via the CC 4.4.3.4.1 Policy-L cascade - every `cohort_scope: self` Contribution's DEK wraps to both, so the app and the agent decrypt the same Self content (memory / config / consent / identity).
config:*.primitive_constraint: config:* SHOULD emit at cohort_scope::SELF (not FEDERATION); CIRISServer's graph_config.rs::config_envelope currently violates this by hardcoding FEDERATION for every row

config:*.rule: A reserved dimension that is inherently a self-report about the emitting entity's own state MUST require attesting_key_id to satisfy a self-referential emitter rule at substrate admission - third-party claims on that prefix about another key are a category error and MUST be rejected, not left to consumer policy.
config:*.cc_ref: CC 3.4.3 (part_3_the_namespace.md:1363-1366), by direct analogy - config:* itself is UNREGISTERED so this rule does not yet apply to it
config:*.quote: A CEG-Conforming Substrate (CCS) MUST reject any incoming `scores` attestation whose `dimension` matches a reserved-prefix pattern below AND whose `attesting_key_id` does not satisfy the prefix's emitter rule.
config:*.primitive_constraint: config:* is currently NOT reserved -> falls to authority_for(unknown)->ProducerSteward with no emitter rule; a third party CAN mint a config:v1 row naming a victim's attested_key_id with no admission-time rejection (CIRISServer's own reconciler is unaffected because its read path additionally filters by attesting_key_id==self, but no OTHER consumer gets that protection for free)

config:*.rule: Riding the single `scores` workhorse primitive for a non-reputational, administrative/config object (rather than inventing a new attestation_type) is an accepted, precedented 1+4-preserving pattern.
config:*.primitive_constraint: config:* riding `scores` with a fixed score:1.0 placeholder is CONSISTENT with precedent, not a violation - no new structural primitive needed; the one part of the family's shape that is already constitutionally sound

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Self-emission AND conflicted-emission forbidden: attester not in {subject, proposed steward, petitioner}
capacity_assurance:*.quote: the subject MUST NOT emit it, and the proposed steward MUST NOT be the attester - a CCS rejects a non-witness or conflicted emitter at admission... No one can self-mint an adult's incapacity, and no one can mint the incapacity of a person they propose to steward.
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: emission/admission composer MUST reject attesting_key_id in {attested_key_id, proposed_steward_key_id, petitioner_key_id} - never sole input from a conflicted party (implemented: check_adult_incapacity_binding `attester_conflicted`)

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Confidence scales with scope - lone-witness attestation never confers continuing/asset power; panel M-of-N independent quorum required for continuing/high-scope domains
capacity_assurance:*.quote: a lone `provider` attestation grants only life-preserving necessity, never asset powers or continuing control... Any continuing or high-scope domain (financial, medical, digital_identity) requires the panel rung - an M-of-N quorum of independent assessors
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: single-witness (provider-rung) attestation MUST NOT be sole input to a continuing-power or asset-bearing delegates_to composer; panel M-of-N independent quorum required

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Reversible-mimic exclusion mandatory before any continuing binding; reversible_pending is a time-boxed T1-only provisional state
capacity_assurance:*.quote: No incapacitated attestation is admissible for a continuing binding until its reversible_excluded companion is present for that domain... the binding MUST lapse if reversible_pending is not resolved to reversible_excluded within the (short) valid_until
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: promote-to-continuing-binding composer requires a reversible_excluded companion per domain; reversible_pending never a permanent carry (implemented: `capacity_reversible_not_excluded`)

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Aggregate FORBIDDEN across domains - capacity is a vector, never collapsed to a scalar
capacity_assurance:*.quote: The capacity-assurance ladder - witness-reserved, per-domain, a vector not a scalar... multiplied per decision-domain because capacity (unlike age) is a multi-dimensional, time-varying, non-monotonic vector
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: aggregate FORBIDDEN - no scalar/global capacity index composed across domains; each domain's band evaluated independently, mirroring testimonial_witness (CC 3.1.9.3) never-aggregated discipline

capacity_assurance:*.quote: misattestation adjudication dimension: moderation:capacity_misattestation // NEVER fires slashing:* alone
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: capacity_assurance misattestation MUST NOT be sole (or any) input to a slashing:* composer; routes exclusively to moderation:* quorum adjudication

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Absence resolves to CAPACITY (presumption of capacity) - inverted from age_assurance's protective-absence default
capacity_assurance:*.quote: Absence resolves to CAPACITY, not protection... this clause resolves absence of a capacity attestation to full capacity / sovereign - the presumption of capacity... Getting this backwards... would be catastrophic; it is forbidden.
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: absence-of-attestation resolver MUST default to capacitated/sovereign per domain; an incapacitated-by-default read is a forbidden inversion (implemented: CapacityState::Unknown -> full capacity)

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Mandatory bounded valid_until + fail-open-to-liberty auto-lapse; steward cannot prolong by silence
capacity_assurance:*.quote: no single valid_until window may exceed the T2 periodic-review cadence... on lapse the binding goes non-live and the adult auto-re-sovereigns with no action required of the recovered person... A steward who wishes to prolong control past the window must put a fresh, attributable, independently-attested renewal on record
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: capacity_assurance-gated delegates_to MUST carry valid_until <= T2_review_cadence and MUST auto-lapse without requiring steward action

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Apophatic floor - protected non-transferable domains never delegable regardless of attested band
capacity_assurance:*.quote: Protected non-transferable domains... contact/visitation..., relational and sexual autonomy, reproduction..., voting, marriage and association, and the dignity-of-risk... These map to the prohibited:* apophatic floor and are carved out of any granted scope.
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: delegates_to scope INTERSECT PROTECTED_NON_TRANSFERABLE MUST = empty regardless of any capacity_assurance band on that domain (implemented: PROTECTED_NON_TRANSFERABLE + scope_touches_protected_domain)

capacity_assurance:*.rule: Restoration/exit-ramp cannot be steward-gated; ward's-champion structurally distinct from steward/assessor/petitioner
capacity_assurance:*.quote: the steward is the conflicted party and may never gate, delay, or be counted in the denominator of a restoration petition... A mandatory ward's-champion... distinct in key from the steward, the assessor, and the petitioner
capacity_assurance:*.primitive_constraint: restoration/withdraws composer MUST NOT accept steward consent as a precondition; ward's-champion key set MUST be disjoint from {steward, assessor, petitioner}

scores:*.rule: Most of the namespace defaults to open-vocabulary emission: anyone may emit a scores attestation on a non-reserved dimension; trust is composed downstream by consumers, not gated at the wire.
scores:*.quote: Most of the namespace is open-vocabulary - anyone may emit, and trust is composed downstream. A small number of prefixes are reserved: only specific identity types may emit them.
scores:*.primitive_constraint: no reserved-prefix admission gate for scores:{domain}; it categorically does NOT inherit capacity:*'s CC 3.4.5 no-self-emit anti-Goodhart rule - self-scoring on a hypothetical scores:medical/scores:safety dimension would be constitutionally admitted today

scores:*.rule: Every leaf value emittable under an open-vocabulary prefix MUST carry an operational definition - a RATCHET calibration package where one applies, or a documented convention otherwise.
scores:*.quote: Every `{axis}` value emittable under open-vocabulary prefixes ... MUST carry an operational definition where the prefix has a calibration package (RATCHET-calibrated detectors) or a documented convention where it doesn't.
scores:*.primitive_constraint: calibration-package-or-documented-convention is a precondition for emit; a hypothetical scores:medical / scores:safety leaf has NEITHER today - no calibration package, and no registry document analogous to WITNESS_KIND_REGISTRY.md - this is the gap that must close before any real emitter ships these leaves.

scores:*.rule: A consent:replication:v1 grant's attestation_prefixes payload array MUST carry CC 3.1-namespace-prefix strings the granting node consents to replicate; trailing ':' is significant and matching is by prefix.
scores:*.quote: `attestation_prefixes` is the [CC 2.6.1] JCS-canonical array of [CC 3.1] namespace-prefix strings G consents to replicate (trailing `:` significant - e.g. `"capacity:"`), sorted ascending + deduplicated, so two implementations holding the same grant agree byte-for-byte.
scores:*.primitive_constraint: each attestation_prefixes entry must name a real, registered-or-open-vocab dimension-namespace prefix. The literal token 'scores:' does NOT name one - it collides with the attestation_type name (CC 2.4.2), not a dimension family. CIRISServer's own production runbook (FSD/BRIDGE_SEED_MESH.md:223) ships attestation_prefixes: ["scores:", "capacity:"], a category-confused value signed into a real, hybrid-signed federation-tier governance object.

scores:*.rule: Open-vocabulary collision discipline for confusingly-similar {kind}/{axis} values within a prefix family: first-registered wins, a Levenshtein-distance guard applies, and an unused-in-90-days value may be reclaimed.
scores:*.quote: First-registered wins for the canonical-attestation surface... Levenshtein-distance guard... No squatting: a `{kind}` registered but never used (no scored attestations in 90 days) MAY be reclaimed.
scores:*.primitive_constraint: governs any FUTURE scores:{domain} leaf collision - not yet triggered; no leaf is registered anywhere in code or docs today.

scores:*.rule: A dimension whose namespace pattern names a subject MUST carry subject_key_ids containing that subject, closing the default-leak failure mode of subject-bearing content publishing without wire-level subject authority.
scores:*.quote: Dimensions whose namespace pattern names a subject MUST carry `subject_key_ids` containing that subject. This closes the default-leak failure mode where subject-bearing content publishes without wire-level subject authority.
scores:*.primitive_constraint: scores:{domain} is NOT among the currently-catalogued subject-bearing patterns. If a scores:medical:{patient_key}:* shape is ever adopted, this catalog MUST be extended before an admission gate can enforce subject-authority presence; today an emitter naming a subject inside a scores:{domain} dimension string with empty subject_key_ids would NOT be caught by this rule.

primitive_gap_report.format: field/primitive: missing processor X in component Y, demanded by [prefixes]

sender.note: Reserved to identity_type=accord_holder; admission requires a THRESHOLD-signed aggregate (2-of-3 genesis; entrenched quorum M/N at scale), never a lone attesting_key_id. Bidirectionally wire-isolated (CC 4.2.1).

data_subject.note: Governance/kill-switch acts about the federation itself; no subject_key_ids anywhere in spec or implementation. resumes_halt_id names a prior halt, not a subject.

recipient_see.note: Every CCC MUST visually distinguish all 4 kinds (CC 4.2.1.2); narrower-than-federation scope defeats the kill switch.

recipient_revoke.note: Only sanctioned reversal of invoke:CONSTITUTIONAL is a separately-thresholded accord:lifecycle:active naming resumes_halt_id; ordinary withdraws/recants by signers are unsupported and unsafe.

transmission_principle.note: Domain-separated anti-replay canonical-bytes discipline substitutes for consent:* grants (CC 4.2.1.1/4.2.1.3).

temporal_lifecycle.note: No per-invocation tombstone lifecycle; lifecycle:active valid_until MUST refresh <=90 days (CC 3.4.1) - reconciled as freshness cap, flagged for maintainer confirmation. Family roster has its own supersedes-based membership lifecycle (CC 4.2.6).

transparency_log:consistency.claim_meaning: Asserts that a producer generated a valid RFC 6962 Merkle consistency proof between two Signed Tree Heads (STH_old at tree_size1 and STH_new at tree_size2) of a transparency log, proving the newer tree is a strict append-only extension of the older one with no rewritten or deleted history.

superset_fields.name: log_id
superset_fields.note: stable identifier of the transparency log (log public-key hash or registered name)

superset_fields.name: tree_size1
superset_fields.note: size (leaf count) of the older tree (STH_old), per RFC 6962

superset_fields.name: tree_size2
superset_fields.note: size of the newer tree (STH_new); tree_size2 > tree_size1

superset_fields.name: sth_old_root_hash
superset_fields.note: root hash of the older tree at tree_size1, from STH_old

superset_fields.name: sth_new_root_hash
superset_fields.note: root hash of the newer tree at tree_size2, from STH_new

superset_fields.name: consistency_proof_nodes
superset_fields.note: ordered Merkle proof node hashes (RFC 6962 PROOF-CONSISTENCY output) enabling independent recomputation

superset_fields.name: verified
superset_fields.note: headline boolean: did local recomputation match both root hashes; drives the pass/fail badge

superset_fields.name: consistency_score
superset_fields.note: confidence backing boolean-via-score: 1.0=freshly verified against directly-fetched STHs; lower=degraded (cached STH, partial proof)

superset_fields.name: sth_old_timestamp
superset_fields.note: timestamp of STH_old, for chain-ordering and staleness

superset_fields.name: sth_new_timestamp
superset_fields.note: timestamp of STH_new

superset_fields.name: prior_claim_ref
superset_fields.note: reference to the preceding consistency claim for the same log_id, forming the proof_chain link

restrictions: recipient_capability per standard cohort ladder (no family-specific override)
log_id SHOULD be globally resolvable for Global projection; otherwise informational-only at Cohort or below
transparency_log:consistency.notes: Boolean-via-score polarity: headline pass/fail (verified) plus consistency_score for partial/degraded states. Consistency claims for the same log_id form a linear proof_chain via prior_claim_ref; a Recanted/Withdrawn claim mid-chain is high-severity. No consent gating; ProducerSteward self-asserts.

A Recanted/Withdrawn claim mid-chain breaks the append-only story (high severity).

constitutional_invariants.rule: The witness-reserved cosigned:* emission MUST NOT occur without a verified consistency proof against the prior STH the witness itself last cosigned (or genesis for a first cosign); Registry MUST reject cosign requests missing consistency_proof_* (MALFORMED_REQUEST) or whose proof doesn't reconstruct both roots (CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID).

constitutional_invariants.quote: witness_quorum_met is therefore quorum on log consistency, not quorum on a string.

constitutional_invariants.rule: A consistency claim is scoped to exactly one log_id instance; per-stream logs (log_id=stream_id) are separate instances from the global provenance log - proofs/STHs from one MUST NOT be cross-verified against another.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: aggregation/chaining MUST partition by log_id; never cross-link distinct log_id values despite the shared RFC mechanism

constitutional_invariants.rule: The RFC 6962-domain-separated construction (CC 5.3.1) is a DISTINCT algorithm from the CEG WholenessWitness self-published state-root scheme (CC 6.1), which lacks append-only/consistency/anti-equivocation guarantees; the two MUST NOT be cross-verified or substituted.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: verify via RFC 6962 0x00/0x01 domain-separated recomputation, never the WW scheme; MUST NOT accept a wholeness_witness:* claim as evidence

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.claim_meaning: A witness has cosigned a specific Signed Tree Head (STH) at a given tree_size, attesting the log is append-only/consistent as of that checkpoint.

superset_fields.name: tree_size
superset_fields.note: tree size at time of cosignature; embedded in the prefix, immutable per-claim key component

superset_fields.name: sth_root_hash
superset_fields.note: Merkle root hash of the STH being cosigned

superset_fields.name: sth_timestamp
superset_fields.note: timestamp of the STH as issued by the log operator

superset_fields.name: witness_identity_ref
superset_fields.note: the witness's federation identity; MUST resolve to identity_type containing 'witness' per CC 3.4.10

superset_fields.name: cosignature
superset_fields.note: the witness's signature over the STH bytes, separate from the base hamburger's own attribution signature

superset_fields.name: log_id
superset_fields.note: identifier of the transparency log instance/region being cosigned

superset_fields.name: prior_sth_ref
superset_fields.note: reference to the previously cosigned STH for this log_id, enabling consistency-proof chaining

superset_fields.name: consistency_proof_verified
superset_fields.note: whether this witness independently verified a consistency proof against prior_sth_ref before cosigning

transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}.notes: Interim substrate-conformance path stores these via a per-region registry_sth_cosignatures table (CC 5.3.1) rather than full CEG-native replication; render a chained timeline of STHs per log_id with witness roster + verification status. Supersede allowed (cosign a newer tree_size); withdraw/recant not meaningful for an append-only witness attestation; delegate not applicable (witness identity non-transferable per CC 3.4.10).

sender.note: Reserved witness-emitter (CC 3.4.10): identity_type SET must contain witness (set-membership, CC 3.4.7.1). Three-way enforced (CC 3.4.7): CCS admission-reject, CCC independent re-check, CCP conformance. CC 5.3.1's independence framing implies witness_relation defaults external, not self.

data_subject.note: Attests about a transparency-log tree state (an STH), not a named identity; dimension pattern names no subject placeholder (CC 4.5.2 test) - subject_key_ids carries no load-bearing entry.

recipient_see.note: CC 5.3.1 anti-equivocation ('a producer cannot show one history to one party and a different one to another') is only meaningful if the proof is broadly visible; the family's design purpose favors the widest practical visibility, narrow self/family scoping being an operator carve-out for private logs, not the natural default.

recipient_revoke.note: Append-only witness fact; no party (including the witness) holds revocation over a past cosignature (FSD: nothing retroactively rewritten). Only forward motion is cosigning a strictly later tree_size, chain-verified per CC 5.3.1.1 - never a retraction.

recipient_receive.note: Public HTTP GET/POST discovery + cosign endpoints - a pull-shaped surface (CC 2.1 default pull); per-stream STH logs (CC 5.3.3.5, push/live_stream) are structurally separate.

information_type.note: {tree_size} is a monotonically-increasing token in the prefix; admission MUST parse and order it per-(witness,log) per CC 5.3.1.1. No reader-side capability gate (the CC 3.4.10 restriction is entirely sender-side).

transmission_principle.note: An independent cryptographic verification act about a log's consistency, not a subject-consented data-sharing arrangement; carries no grants/audience/valid_until of its own.

temporal_lifecycle.note: CC 2.6.7 pins a family-specific freshness rule: cosignatures whose signed_at is farther than 5 min from the STH's published signed_at MUST be rejected - two distinct timestamps whose difference admission MUST bound. Forward-only: supersedes = cosigning a strictly-later tree_size, chain-verified against the witness's own prior cosigned STH. No deletion window (append-only integrity primitive).

constitutional_invariants.rule: transparency_log:cosigned:* is witness-reserved: attesting_key_id.identity_type SET must contain witness (set-membership); rejected at admission (CCS), re-checked at consumption (CCC), forbidden at production (CCP).
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: emitter reservation - non-witness attesting_key_id REJECTED at admission, not merely advisory

sender.note: Emitter class is polymorphic PER LEAF, not fixed for the family - CC 3.3.1's table names a different emitter for nearly every row: subject_key_id for consent:state:granted/revoked, consent:scope:*, consent:partnership_grant, consent:stream:*; producer for consent:deletion_sla/deletion_complete, consent:partnership_accept; substrate(Persist) for consent:state:expired and consent:decay:*; the granting NODE itself for consent:replication:{version}. Persist's own consent_grammar.rs code comment states the Nissenbaum mapping directly: 'sender -> attesting_key_id (who authored the grant)'. No CC 3.4 reserved-prefix row constrains who may be attesting_key_id for any consent:* leaf.

data_subject.note: For the common case (CC 3.3.1 composition pattern) subject_key_ids names the PERSON the target Contribution's consent state concerns -- a genuine data_subject. For consent:replication:{version} (CC 3.3.7) the SAME field is repurposed to name the RECIPIENT PEER NODE ([P]), not a person. This is a real overload: one wire field plays the data_subject role in one branch of the family and a recipient-designation role in another.

recipient_see.note: Default/open per CC 2.3.3 for consent:state/scope/stream/deletion_sla/deletion_complete/partnership_*. CC 3.3.7 pins cohort_scope="federation" as MANDATORY for consent:replication:{version} specifically -- 'the grant itself is a public governance record'. CIRISServer's producer-side emit_replication_consent (src/peer.rs) hardcodes cohort_scope:"federation" at emission, but NO admission-time check in CIRISPersist re-verifies a received consent:replication grant actually carries cohort_scope=federation -- producer discipline only, not substrate-enforced.

recipient_revoke.note: This IS the family's central function for the common case: consent:* dimensions are the wire-level exercise of CC 2.4.1.1 subject-revocation authority (rules 2/3/4) over a target Contribution T, implemented at CIRISPersist src/federation/admission.rs#resolve_withdraws_admission_rule. CC 4.4.3.5.4 pins the composition discipline: ANY ONE subject in T.subject_key_ids revoking is terminal for ALL subjects (OR-composition, explicitly NEVER majority/quorum-softened) -- confirmed implemented (subject_key_ids.iter().any(...), no quorum counting). For consent:replication, by contrast, the named peer in subject_key_ids holds NO revocation authority over the grant -- only the granting node G can withdraws its own grant.

recipient_receive.note: consent:* dimensions do not touch or override delivery_mode; it rides the CC 2.3.3 default (pull, or push per CC 5.3.3) untouched. consent:replication is delivery-ADJACENT in effect but acts through payload.attestation_prefixes filtering promotion/serve eligibility (CIRISPersist#509/#510, CIRISEdge#396) rather than the delivery_mode envelope field.

information_type.note: consent:* is explicitly OPEN VOCABULARY per CC 3.3.1 ('Open vocabulary per CC 4.5.1.1; canonical kinds named here') -- not RATCHET-calibrated. BUT unlike testimonial_witness (which has WITNESS_KIND_REGISTRY.md), the Constitution names NO discoverability registry document for new consent:{kind} leaves -- a real documentation gap. attestation_prefixes further narrows information_type to an explicit namespace-prefix SET on the wire; consent_grammar.rs#covers() is the mechanical processor, and consent_transferability() exhaustively classifies which EnvelopeKinds may appear in payload.kinds (Attestation is Consentable; all 12 structural-plane kinds are not -- a 15th kind added without updating this match is a compile failure, the good pattern this family should be judged against).

transmission_principle.note: THE central axis for this family, and persist's own code says so verbatim (consent_grammar.rs: 'the fifth [Nissenbaum axis] -- transmission-principle -- is the consent:* dimension family itself'). CC 3.3.1's consent:scope:{kind} canonical kinds (retain/share/analyze/train/publish) are reified byte-for-byte as the closed TransmissionPrinciple enum in ConsentTransferPolicy. Restrictions (RecipientCapability, StripField) are a second-order refinement unique to consent:replication, with a DELIBERATE split enforcement point: RecipientCapability at SERVE (CIRISEdge bridge.rs#recipient_capability_withholds), StripField at PROMOTION (persist consent_grammar.rs#strip_field).

temporal_lifecycle.note: Heavily elaborated, with THREE distinct composed lifecycle mechanisms: (1) CC 4.4.3.5.2 deletion-SLA watcher (hard_case.rs#run_consent_sla_watch / parse_deletion_sla_days); (2) CC 5.3.2.2 promotion-SLA (list_consent_revocation_promotion_overdue) is a SEPARATE 24h clock specific to this family -- a subject-side revocation may transit local-tier but must never REST there, and both clocks read one shared signal so they can't desync (AV-61 closure); (3) CC 4.4.3.5.1 consent:decay:{stage} is a third independent multi-stage anonymization-milestone emission keyed on a producer-published decay_protocol string. recants is explicitly FORBIDDEN as a subject-side lifecycle vehicle (CC 2.4.1.1).
