deltas_from_seed: The seed's "cc_section": "UNREGISTERED" overstates the gap: the family is thoroughly, normatively specified at CC 3.3.1, CC 3.3.5, CC 3.3.7, CC 4.4.3.5/Policy K, and CC 4.5.2 -- roughly 300+ lines of normative prose plus a working reference implementation in CIRISPersist and CIRISEdge. What is actually unregistered is narrower and mechanical: the family has no row in the CC-3.1-scoped machine-readable manifest that CIRISPersist's authority_for() reads. Correct framing: 'absent from the CC-3.1 vendored namespace manifest', not 'absent from the Constitution'.

Root-caused the fallback: tools/build_cc_namespace.py is DELIBERATELY scoped to `### 3.1.1`-`### 3.1.10` headings only. consent:* lives under the sibling top-level heading CC 3.3, structurally never in the generator's walk. The ProducerSteward fallback is a tooling-scope gap dating to when CC 3.3 was added, not a constitutional silence.

The seed's prescription 'MUST be deliberately reserved-classed' is corrected: CC 3.3.1 explicitly classifies this family as OPEN vocabulary -- reserving the whole family would break the common case. The right fix is per-leaf: register the family as open, add two reserved-class sub-rows for the two genuinely substrate-only leaves (consent:state:expired, consent:decay:{stage}; persist's class_for() already has the SubstrateSelf mapping mechanism, just no manifest row to trigger it), plus the missing admission-time enforcement for consent:replication's structural constraints.

The seed's implicit single "polarity": "n/a" is wrong at the per-leaf level: CC 3.3.1's table gives a DIFFERENT polarity per leaf -- enumerated (consent:state:*), signed (consent:deletion_sla, consent:replication), positive-only (consent:deletion_complete, consent:partnership_grant/accept), enumerated (consent:stream:*, consent:scope:*, consent:decay:*). The registry row needs a per-leaf polarity column.

The seed's single "owning_component": "persist" flattens a genuinely cross-cutting family: emitters vary by leaf across ordinary federation members, producers, substrate (persist), and nodes. Evidence the NamespaceEntry schema's one-owning-component-per-family assumption does not fit a CC 3.3 family whose whole point is multi-actor emission.

constitution-silent (honest gap, not invented): the Constitution does not explicitly re-state the CC 1.2 T4 'never sole evidence for slashing:*' discipline specifically for consent:* attestations anywhere found.

documentation gap (not a reserved-prefix gap): CC 4.5.1.1 names WITNESS_KIND_REGISTRY.md for open-vocab testimonial_witness/hard_case leaves, but no equivalent registry document is named for new operator-coined consent:{kind} leaves.

data_subject.note: delegates_to carries no subject_key_ids. The party actually gated by this family - the node whose federated capabilities the trust_root_valid() predicate switches on/off - is NEITHER the sender NOR a named subject NOR the attested_key_id of the edge; it is discovered indirectly by walking the separate owner-binding graph. A real CI gap: the most consequential party has no first-class position in the envelope at all.

recipient_see.note: Unpinned by the FSD. The charter SHOULD default to cohort_scope: federation/Commons-plaintext by analogy to CC 3.2's infrastructure-community rule ('the trust root cannot be an opaque blob... structural-invisibility does NOT apply'), but nothing enforces this. The individual user's trust edge visibility is wholly unspecified, yet CIRISEdge#386 leg B requires a peer to confirm 'the recipient's infra:serve roots to a root the sending node itself trusts' - which requires the edge be visible to that peer.

recipient_revoke.note: Governed by CC 2.4.1.1's four authority paths. Because delegates_to carries no subject_key_ids, only rule 1 (producer self-withdraw) applies by default: the trust edge is revocable ONLY by the user who signed it (asymmetric - the root cannot revoke the user's trust of it, which is correct and load-bearing). The charter is revocable only by the root itself, EXCEPT the m-of-n pre-committed recovery ceremony (check_trust_charter_admission) lets a DIFFERENT, pre-committed successor key supersede a compromised charter - a bespoke 5th revocation shape not enumerated anywhere in CC 2.4.1.1.

What IS new/unregistered is the semantic overlay: 'serve+attest is the validity minimum for root-hood', and store/transport being charter-grantable while network_presence/hold_*_membership are deliberately owner-only - none of this split is in ratified CC text.

transmission_principle.note: CC 3.2 states explicitly: 'Trust is inbound - accepting what a member produces; consent is outbound - letting one's own data flow to a member... sender.note: MUST be the claimed owner's OWN key - CC 3.2 line 501 'The owner signs its own owner-binding (MUST) ... owner == delegates_to.attesting_key_id'. This is the mirror image of the registry's existing 'no-self-emit' reserved_rule: ownership REQUIRES self-attestation on the claiming side. CIRISServer's build_owner_binding_envelope enforces this by construction (the responsible user's own LocalSigner signs, never the node's). The genesis binding is additionally co-signed by/carried in the node's own provisioning record so a remote party cannot front-run an unclaimed node.

data_subject.note: The generic CI rubric's subject_key_ids axis is UNUSED. The delegation's target (the owned node/agent key) rides a distinct field - node_key_id at the server wire layer, attested_key_id in persist's row - not subject_key_ids. This matters: the owned node/agent has NO independent revocation authority over its own ownership row (it is node-role, no agency per CC 4.4.3.4.3), so the standard rule-2 subject-withdraws path does not apply here at all. Confirmed empty in the actual wire builder.

recipient_see.note: Defaults to cohort_scope: self (CC 5.2 structural invisibility) and is explicitly promotable to cohort_scope: federation for public accountability via the CC 4.4.3.3.1 supersedes-promotion pattern (promote_owner_binding_to_federation, 'self-balancing ownership', CIRISServer#125). A self-scoped binding additionally self-replicates across the owner's other identity_occurrences per the CC 5.2 self-cohort composition rule.

recipient_revoke.note: NOT subject_key_ids-mediated. Revocation authority is: (a) the incumbent owner's own withdraws/recants (CC 2.4.1.1 rule 1); or (b) - per CC 3.2's 'No permanent ownerless lock (MUST)' - a Wise-Authority/recovery authority on an adjudicated finding of provable death or seizure. Path (b) is stated as a MUST at the policy level but no concrete withdraws-admission-rule covers a third party revoking a LIVE incumbent's binding without a pre-existing delegation from that incumbent. CIRISPersist v21.4.0 confirms: only the self-withdraw path is implemented; grep across src/ and tests/ finds zero occurrences of 'seizure', 'reclaim', 'provably.dead', or 'ownerless'. The family's most significant gap.

recipient_receive.note: No family-specific override found; inherits the base self/family key-grant cascade (CC 4.4.3.4.1) for self-scoped delivery, widening to federation-tier ingest on promotion.

information_type.note: dimension = 'ownership:responsible_party:node:v1'. The load-bearing restriction is the CC 4.4.3.4.3 reserved two-prefix scope split: a delegates_to whose target key resolves to a node-only identity_type MUST carry ONLY infra:* delegated_scope values; agency:* is FORBIDDEN and wire-rejected (Error::NodeAgencyForbidden, check_node_agency_admission). This is the wire-checkable form of 'infrastructure must not have agency'.

transmission_principle.note: Ownership binding is NOT a consent:* object. Its consent-analog is structural: the owner's OWN signature over the delegates_to envelope IS the claim of ownership/responsibility (CC 3.2 line 501, mirroring the minor-stewardship rule's 'signature IS the agreement-to-stewardship'). The nearest wire analog to a consent valid_until is delegation_valid_until, which CC 3.2 line 503 says SHOULD be set so a binding can lapse rather than locking a node ownerless forever - and this lapse check IS implemented.

temporal_lifecycle.note: delegation_valid_until SHOULD be set (CC 3.2) and IS lapse-enforced in persist. Ownership TRANSFER is explicitly supersede-then-rebind or withdraw-then-rebind, NEVER accretive (CC 3.2 line 502 'Admission-time enforcement (MUST)') - enforced by check_single_node_owner_admission rejecting any second distinct-owner binding while one is live (Error::NodeAlreadyOwned), wired into all three CIRISPersist backends. recants does not apply to ownership transfer semantics. deletion_window has no stated analog for owner-bindings; the closest is the WA-adjudicated liveness/seizure finding, which is adjudicatory, not SLA-timed, and has no implemented wire path yet.

constitutional_invariants.rule: A node/agent key is owner-bound by AT MOST ONE responsible steward at any time; owner_of MUST resolve to at most one key and MUST NOT be resolved by picking off a sorted/lexicographic set on cardinality>1 - it is a hard fail-closed error, not a tie-break.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: owner_of/single-owner resolution FORBIDDEN from using aggregate, majority, or deterministic-pick composition; cardinality != 1 -> fail-closed. IMPLEMENTED: owner_of returns Error::AmbiguousNodeOwner on cardinality>1; check_single_node_owner_admission rejects a second distinct owner AT admission time.

constitutional_invariants.rule: The owner-binding's attesting_key_id MUST equal the claimed owner (self-attestation is the claim of ownership); the FIRST (genesis) binding is additionally set at provisioning, not decided by who reaches the substrate first.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: sender == claimed-owner REQUIRED (self-emit required, inverse of the registry's existing no-self-emit reserved_rule pattern). IMPLEMENTED: build_owner_binding_envelope/build_signed_owner_binding signs with the responsible user's own LocalSigner.

constitutional_invariants.rule: While a live owner-binding exists, the substrate MUST reject a second, distinct-owner binding at bind time; the incumbent must withdraws/recants first (or lapse). Ownership transfer is explicit, never accretive.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: delegates_to(delegation_purpose=owner_binding) admission is NOT append/accrete. IMPLEMENTED: check_single_node_owner_admission -> Error::NodeAlreadyOwned, wired into memory/sqlite/postgres put_attestation.

constitutional_invariants.rule: No permanent ownerless lock: a key rendered ownerless by a provably-dead incumbent MUST remain re-claimable via WA/recovery-authority-adjudicated liveness finding; the SAME recovery authority MAY also withdraw a binding found to be a live wrongful seizure.

sender.note: Wire: attesting_key_id. CIRISServer's impl (src/graph_config.rs set_config/config_envelope) hardcodes attesting_key_id = the NODE's own derived federation key - never the human owner's personal identity_key. The human owner only authenticates at the HTTP layer (SYSTEM_ADMIN session, config_api.rs require_owner); the NODE signs on their behalf. This is a self-loop self-report shape (attesting_key_id == attested_key_id == node_key_id, verified by list_attestations_by which filters by attesting_key_id - so third-party injection of config ABOUT this node is structurally blocked today). But because config:* is NOT a reserved prefix, nothing stops a THIRD PARTY from emitting its own config:v1 scores row naming attested_key_id = some OTHER (victim) node - no reserved emitter rule requires self-loop, so any generic consumer that queries 'attestations about node X' (list_attestations_for) rather than 'authored by node X' could be shown spoofed config claims with no admission-time rejection.

data_subject.note: Wire: subject_key_ids is always set to [node_key_id] - purely self-referential. The ACTUAL semantic subject of a row (which config key, or in federation_peers.rs's reuse, which PEER a sideband trust/appearance/SAS annotation is about) lives only in the untyped envelope['key'] string (e.g. 'federation.peer_sideband.<peer_key_id>'), never in subject_key_ids. A peer named inside such a key-string has no structural subject_key_ids presence at all - they cannot exercise CI axis-4 (recipient_revoke) over a record substantively about them, by design (private local operator annotations, not federated claims) - but this also means no generic CI-aware tool can find/audit 'every record about peer P' by scanning subject_key_ids.

recipient_see.note: THE HEADLINE FINDING. src/graph_config.rs config_envelope() hardcodes cohort_scope: cohort_scope::FEDERATION for every config:v1 row, with a comment claiming 'federation is the closed-set cohort the substrate admits for a federation-tier row' - but this codebase already uses cohort_scope::SELF for exactly this kind of node-local, owner-only record (src/claim_remote.rs:829, 'bind it self-scoped by default (no federation announce until the owner opts in)'). Per CIRISPersist's own cohort_scope module, SELF/FAMILY are the ONLY scopes that are 'structurally invisible' (suppresses_holds_bytes==true); FEDERATION is the broadest-visibility default. Config rows - including auth.admin_key_ids, net.bootstrap_peers, and federation.peer_sideband.<peer> trust/appearance/SAS-verification annotations - are emitted at the ONE cohort_scope value persist explicitly does NOT structurally protect. CC 4.4.3.4.3 independently corroborates that 'config' as a content class is contemplated at cohort_scope:self. The ONLY thing currently preventing replication to a federation peer is that DEFAULT_GRANT_ATTESTATION_PREFIXES (src/peer.rs:49) defaults to just ['capacity:'] - safety rests entirely on an operator not naming 'config' in a POST /v1/federation/peering attestation_prefixes list, a discretionary consumer-policy control, not a wire/substrate guarantee.

recipient_revoke.note: config_key_revoked() honors withdraws/recants authored by node_key_id against the row's attestation_id, or a revocations_for hit - only the node itself can revoke a config row. Internally consistent for the node's OWN operational config. For the federation_peers.rs peer-sideband reuse (a config:v1 row semantically ABOUT another peer), that peer has zero revoke authority over the annotation naming them - acceptable given these are private local operator judgments, but CI axis-4 as normally construed does not apply to the semantic subject here, only to the node/author.

recipient_receive.note: No distinct delivery_mode concept - config:v1 rows are PULLED on demand (GET /v1/config, or config_reconcile.rs's periodic resolve()), never pushed to a named recipient set. The only 'delivery' that matters is the cohort_scope/replication-consent path covered under recipient_see.

information_type.note: Wire: dimension is a FLAT constant 'config:v1' for every row regardless of what the row is about (a runtime cadence knob vs. auth.admin_key_ids vs. a peer trust override) - the true information_type discriminator (the config KEY) lives ONLY in the untyped envelope['key'] JSON string, invisible to any dimension-based admission policy, reserved-prefix check, or per-key sensitivity rule. Contrast with the precedented watchlist:{id} shape where {id} rides IN the dimension string, making it admission-visible. Recommend hoisting the key into the dimension leaf (config:{key}) or a typed EnvelopeCore field.

transmission_principle.note: No consent:* grant machinery attaches to config:v1 rows - config is self-retained node data, not shared/retained/analyzed/trained/published under any grants() framework. Coherent AS LONG AS cohort_scope stays self/family. If a config row ever crosses into an operator's attestation_prefixes replication grant, it would flow to a peer with ZERO transmission-principle framing at all, compounding the severity of that leak path.

temporal_lifecycle.note: asserted_at is set on every write; no valid_until is ever set - config rows are asserted to live forever until explicitly superseded. Lifecycle uses a CUSTOM app-level version/previous_version chain (both untyped extra fields) that duplicates persist's typed EnvelopeCore.references_attestation_id / the structural supersedes composer ('There is no substrate supersede-aware reader yet ... the version-fold already gives last-write-wins for the common path'). Deletion is dual-path: (a) an app-level tombstone - a fresh row with value=ConfigValue::Null, recognized ONLY by config.rs-aware readers - invisible to any generic CEG consumer; and (b) genuine withdraws/recants against the attestation_id, which IS structurally visible fabric-wide. (a) should be replaced or accompanied by (b).

constitutional_invariants.rule: Config-class content ('memory / config / consent / identity') is normatively cohort_scope:self, DEK-wrapped via the CC 4.4.3.4.1 Policy-L key-grant cascade, and shared identically between a Self's occurrences - not a federation-tier broadcast.

constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: calibration-package-or-documented-convention is a precondition for emit; a hypothetical scores:medical / scores:safety leaf has NEITHER today - no calibration package, and no registry document analogous to WITNESS_KIND_REGISTRY.md - this is the gap that must close before any real emitter ships these leaves.
constitutional_invariants.quote: Every `{axis}` value emittable under open-vocabulary prefixes ... MUST carry an operational definition where the prefix has a calibration package (RATCHET-calibrated detectors) or a documented convention where it doesn't.

constitutional_invariants.rule: A consent:replication:v1 grant's attestation_prefixes payload array MUST carry CC 3.1-namespace-prefix strings the granting node consents to replicate; trailing ':' is significant and matching is by prefix.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: each attestation_prefixes entry must name a real, registered-or-open-vocab dimension-namespace prefix. The literal token 'scores:' does NOT name one - it collides with the attestation_type name (CC 2.4.2), not a dimension family. CIRISServer's own production runbook (FSD/BRIDGE_SEED_MESH.md:223) ships attestation_prefixes: ["scores:", "capacity:"], a category-confused value signed into a real, hybrid-signed federation-tier governance object.
constitutional_invariants.quote: `attestation_prefixes` is the [CC 2.6.1] JCS-canonical array of [CC 3.1] namespace-prefix strings G consents to replicate (trailing `:` significant - e.g. `"capacity:"`), sorted ascending + deduplicated, so two implementations holding the same grant agree byte-for-byte.

constitutional_invariants.rule: Open-vocabulary collision discipline for confusingly-similar {kind}/{axis} values within a prefix family: first-registered wins, a Levenshtein-distance guard applies, and an unused-in-90-days value may be reclaimed.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: governs any FUTURE scores:{domain} leaf collision - not yet triggered; no leaf is registered anywhere in code or docs today.
constitutional_invariants.quote: First-registered wins for the canonical-attestation surface... Levenshtein-distance guard... No squatting: a `{kind}` registered but never used (no scored attestations in 90 days) MAY be reclaimed.

constitutional_invariants.rule: A dimension whose namespace pattern names a subject MUST carry subject_key_ids containing that subject, closing the default-leak failure mode of subject-bearing content publishing without wire-level subject authority.
constitutional_invariants.primitive_constraint: scores:{domain} is NOT among the currently-catalogued subject-bearing patterns. If a scores:medical:{patient_key}:* shape is ever adopted, this catalog MUST be extended before an admission gate can enforce subject-authority presence; today an emitter naming a subject inside a scores:{domain} dimension string with empty subject_key_ids would NOT be caught by this rule.
constitutional_invariants.quote: Dimensions whose namespace pattern names a subject MUST carry `subject_key_ids` containing that subject. This closes the default-leak failure mode where subject-bearing content publishes without wire-level subject authority.

registry_coverage_gap.scope: the 9 families that are LIVE (or live-adjacent) in production but carry no row in the 95-family CC-1.0-rc2 namespace registry

root_cause.scope_boundary: the generator walks ONLY '### 3.1.N' per-owning-component headings (its docstring says so: 'Section CC 3.1 (### 3.1.1 ... ### 3.1.10, minus the 3.1.7 summary) catalogs the prefix families by owning component').
root_cause.consequence: every family defined under a SIBLING top-level heading is structurally invisible to the manifest: CC 3.2 (ownership/trust-root/steward-binding), CC 3.3 (content-ingestion prefixes incl. the whole consent:* family), CC 3.4.11/3.4.12 (age_assurance / capacity_assurance). This is a tooling-scope gap dating to when CC 3.3 was added, NOT constitutional silence and NOT a deliberate 'leave this open' decision.
root_cause.dead_code_tell: build_cc_namespace.py's RESERVED_RULES table already contains a capacity_assurance predicate - it can never fire, because the heading-regex extractor never yields that family. The generator's own author expected the row to exist.

producer_steward_fallback_risk.mechanism: CIRISPersist src/federation/namespace/registry.rs#authority_for() returns ProducerSteward with reserved:None for any dimension with no manifest row; class_for() only special-cases the 'substrate-self-report' rule token, so every OTHER reserved rule collapses to ProducerSteward regardless of registry presence.
producer_steward_fallback_risk.blast_radius_today: PRIMARILY METADATA LOSS, not an open admission hole - because (a) no consumer currently branches on `.reserved` for a live decision, and (b) the two families with real enforcement needs (capacity_assurance:*, ownership:*) are gated by hand-maintained admission code that does not consult authority_for() at all.
producer_steward_fallback_risk.the_real_risk: SPLIT TRUTH. There are now two independent answers to 'is this prefix reserved, and to whom?' inside one crate: the hand-maintained admission gates (admission.rs#default_reserved_prefix_rules, #check_adult_incapacity_binding, #check_single_node_owner_admission, #check_trace_dimension_admission) and the CC-3.1-generated classifier (namespace/registry.rs#authority_for). They have already diverged for capacity_assurance:*. Any future consumer that trusts the generated classifier - a policy engine, a UI badge, a replication filter - will read 'open, unreserved, ProducerSteward' for a witness-reserved clinical-capacity family.
producer_steward_fallback_risk.second_order_risk: config:* is the one family where the fallback is directly exploitable today: it is unreserved, so nothing in the substrate rejects a THIRD party minting a config:v1 row naming a victim node's attested_key_id. CIRISServer's own reconciler is immune only because its read path additionally filters attesting_key_id==self; no other consumer of the corpus inherits that protection.
producer_steward_fallback_risk.non_risk: trace:*, trace_summary:*, and the common case of consent:* are CORRECTLY open-vocabulary. Reserving them wholesale would break the common case (any federation member must be able to self-emit consent about their own data; any agent must be able to emit its own reasoning trace). The fix is per-leaf, not blanket.

proposed_registry_rows.reserved_rule: OPEN family with two substrate-only sub-rows: consent:state:expired and consent:decay:{stage} MUST be SubstrateSelf (persist's class_for() already has the mapping; only the manifest row is missing)
proposed_registry_rows.polarity: PER-LEAF (enumerated | signed | positive-only) - a single family-wide polarity column cannot represent CC 3.3.1's own table
proposed_registry_rows.schema_note: the NamespaceEntry one-owning-component-per-family assumption (inherited from the CC 3.1 per-component model) does not fit a CC 3.3 family whose whole point is multi-actor emission (subject / producer / substrate / node). Surfacing this to whoever extends the generator matters more than the value chosen.
proposed_registry_rows.description: Transmission-principle family. Normatively specified across ~300 lines of CC 3.3.1/3.3.5/3.3.7 + Policy K (CC 4.4.3.5.x) with a working reference implementation; what is unregistered is the manifest row, NOT the constitution.

proposed_registry_rows.reserved_rule: self-emission MANDATORY (attesting_key_id MUST appear in subject_key_ids) - the exact structural mirror of CC 3.4.5's capacity:* anti-self-emission REJECTION
proposed_registry_rows.polarity: n/a (existence record, not a graded verdict - every mint site sets weight: None)
proposed_registry_rows.description: Sealed reasoning trace. persist's admission.rs:1291-1295 already states in-source that the registry entry + validator are 'pending CC ratification' - the code knows it is ahead of the constitution. Normative weight is split across four repos (persist=admission+promotion, edge=serve gate, server=consent route+policy-hash pin, agent/lens-core=capture/scrub/seal); a single owning_component undersells it.

NOT A PREFIX. trace_manifest:v1 is the value of a `schema` key inside a nested manifest object - one of two mutually exclusive payload shapes inside a trace:complete:v1 envelope, selected when canonical bytes exceed MAX_ATTESTATION_ENVELOPE_BYTES. Same category as CC 8.4.2.1's c2pa_manifest evidence_refs.kind: payload-level, not wire-level. Carried in this manifest as a family row ONLY so the round-1 seed card that proposed it has a place to record its correction.

proposed_registry_rows.polarity: n/a (multi-field feature vector, no single polarity)
proposed_registry_rows.description: Denormalized scorer-input feature vector. Registering it matters for ONE reason above all: CC 3.3.7's trailing-colon-significant prefix matching means a grant scoped to 'trace:' does NOT cover 'trace_summary:'. Without a registry row, an operator has no discoverable way to learn that the scorer-input surface needs its own explicit attestation_prefixes entry.

proposed_registry_rows.cc_section: PROPOSE a new CC 2.4.1.x subsection (parallel to CC 2.4.1.2's owner_binding treatment)

The literal 'trust:*' dimension strings that DO exist (trust:demo:v1, trust:reliability:v1) are test placeholders. Registering the placeholder would enshrine the wrong thing.

Registering it makes the ALREADY-ENFORCED rule legible to authority_for() consumers and closes the split-truth risk before a second reader appears.

proposed_registry_rows.polarity: boolean-via-score (fixed 1.0 placeholder; presence-of-live-row is the signal)

Fix EITHER by extending build_cc_namespace.py to walk CC 3.3.x/3.4.x embedded families, OR by hand-appending capacity_assurance + age_assurance as two explicitly-non-generated catalog rows.

The seed card's illustrative leaves (scores:medical, scores:safety) exist nowhere in code, and its 'lens' owning_component is unsupported (crates/ciris-lens-core/src/scores/ is an unrelated self-read facade over DetectionEvent rows). field_standardization.purpose: THE COMPRESSION PASS. Same field => same processor, by registry rule rather than review vigilance. A new family REFERENCES a canonical field + its standard_relationship instead of re-specifying a processor.
field_standardization.scope_note: 0.3.0 clusters are drawn from the 9 UNREGISTERED families and cross-linked to already-registered demanders where the alias is exact. Back-filling clusters across all 104 families is a 0.4.0 task.

tiers.universal: EnvelopeCore/Attestation-base; present on every claim; ONE processor, no opt-out
tiers.standard: registry-defined shared field; opt-in per family; ONE processor wherever carried
tiers.bespoke: family cargo; no processor; MUST NOT be silently promoted to standard

clusters.semantics: who can SEE. `audience` inside a consent grant is not a different field - it is the PRE-STAMP form of cohort_scope, which promote_consented_backlog copies onto the promoted row.
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying `audience` OBLIGATES the promoter to stamp it into cohort_scope and OBLIGATES the emitter to accept that the row's visibility is grant-derived, not producer-chosen. Carrying cohort_scope in {self, family} OBLIGATES structural invisibility (no holds_bytes row, no propagation).
clusters.asymmetry_note: consent narrows, never widens: a grant's audience may only tighten what a producer already permitted.
rename_flags: consent:*/trace:* `audience` SHOULD be documented as an alias of cohort_scope, not a distinct concept

clusters.semantics: the party the claim is ABOUT, and therefore the party holding CC 2.4.1.1 rule-2 revocation authority.
clusters.standard_relationship: naming a party here CONFERS revocation authority on them - which is why ownership:* and capacity_assurance:* deliberately do NOT use it (the owned node has no agency; the ward's revocation route is the restoration petition, not a wire withdraws), and why config:* burying a peer id in an untyped key string means no CI-aware tool can enumerate 'every record about peer P'.
clusters.asymmetry_note: conferral is one-way: adding a subject can only ADD revocation authority, never remove the producer's. Also forfeits local-tier eligibility (CC 5.3.2.4.1) - a deliberate cost.
rename_flags: config:*: hoist the semantic subject out of extra.key into subject_key_ids OR document explicitly that these are non-claims about third parties

clusters.semantics: temporal UPPER bound - after this instant the claim is as dead as a withdrawn one.
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying it OBLIGATES expiry-as-tombstone (already true for delegates_to since persist v19.0.0) and, where a review cadence exists, OBLIGATES the bound to be <= that cadence. It does NOT obligate an active sweep - and capacity_assurance:* is the family where that omission is load-bearing.
clusters.asymmetry_note: expiry must fail toward LESS authority (capacity_assurance's fail-open-to-liberty is the sharpest case); an implementation that treats a lapsed bound as 'still live pending review' inverts the axiom.

clusters.tier: universal (PROPOSED - does not exist on the wire)
clusters.semantics: temporal LOWER bound, dual to valid_until. See the freshness_floor section.
clusters.processor: PROPOSED - monotonic-max merge + signed touch-claim; no processor exists today
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying it OBLIGATES monotonic-max merge and admission rejection of any value > now+skew; it NEVER substitutes for a family's own renewal requirement.
clusters.asymmetry_note: monotonic max is deliberately one-directional (anti-rollback); a 'latest wins' merge that could DECREASE the floor would let a stale replica resurrect a dead liveness claim.

clusters.semantics: the universal tombstone/target link: what this claim replaces, retracts, or repairs.
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying a supersede/withdraw relation OBLIGATES using this typed field rather than a private chain. config:*'s custom version/previous_version pair is the exemplar violation: it re-implements a typed primitive in untyped extra, so only config-aware readers can follow the chain.
clusters.asymmetry_note: anti-rollback: retraction projects Global and must OUTRUN assertion; a private chain that only one module can read defeats that by construction.
rename_flags: config:* version/previous_version -> RENAME onto references_attestation_id + supersedes

clusters.semantics: the prefix set a node consents to replicate; trailing ':' significant, matched by exact string prefix against `dimension`.
clusters.processor: CIRISPersist/src/federation/consent_grammar.rs#covers - the ONE processor, consumed at promotion (persist) and at serve (edge)
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying an entry OBLIGATES that the entry names a real dimension namespace. It does NOT obligate transitivity: 'trace:' covering 'trace_summary:' is FORBIDDEN by construction. An entry that can never match any dimension is a defect the author-time validator must reject.
clusters.asymmetry_note: non-transitive by design; 'helpfully' widening the match to include derivative prefixes would silently export a surface the operator never granted.

aliases.alias_name: extra.scope (ConfigScope) - FALSE FRIEND, not this field

clusters.semantics: capability tokens carried on a delegation; infra:* vs agency:* is a reserved two-prefix split.
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying a node-only target OBLIGATES infra:*-only scopes and attenuation (child subset of parent). Carrying infra:serve OBLIGATES the holder be a pure node-role delegate with NO agency:* on the same delegation.
clusters.asymmetry_note: 'infrastructure must not have agency' is deliberately one-directional: agency keys may be denied infra scopes by policy, but infra keys are CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY denied agency.
rename_flags: config:* `scope` (ConfigScope::Local|Identity) collides with the typed EnvelopeCore.scope path - RENAME to config_scope

aliases.alias_name: (absent - the family does not set or check it)

clusters.semantics: which sub-relation a delegates_to edge expresses; the ONLY discriminator that makes purpose-filtered reads (owner_of) sound.
clusters.standard_relationship: any purpose-filtered graph read OBLIGATES filtering on this field, not on a family-internal dimension string. CIRISPersist#378 is the precedent: the internal-dimension-only gate was bypassable via emit_attestation_self until delegation_purpose was added as a second discriminator.
clusters.asymmetry_note: trust:* reads delegates_to edges WITHOUT purpose-filtering, so a bare act-on-behalf edge can satisfy a trust-root check - the same class of bug #378 fixed for ownership.

clusters.semantics: a sha256 commitment to bytes or to a contract.
clusters.processor: CIRISPersist/src/trace_summary_contract.rs#extraction_manifest_sha256 (contract form); NO processor for the content form
clusters.standard_relationship: carrying a content commitment OBLIGATES a resolvable retrieval path OR an explicit declaration that the row is integrity-only and NOT content-equivalent. trace_manifest:* carries the commitment with neither - the gap.
clusters.asymmetry_note: commitment without retrieval is a one-directional hash: verifiable if you already have the bytes, useless if you do not.

clusters.semantics: who authored the claim - and, for a whole class of families, the field an equality check runs against.
clusters.standard_relationship: a family MUST declare its self-emission polarity: REQUIRED (ownership:*, trace:*, config:* proposed), FORBIDDEN (capacity:*, capacity_assurance:*), or OPEN. Silence is not a third option - it is how config:* ended up spoofable.
clusters.asymmetry_note: the two polarities are mirror axioms, not a convention: anti-Goodhart forbids self-emission where a score confers advantage; self-attestation is REQUIRED where the claim IS the act of taking responsibility.

duality_audit.principle: Mechanism must be closed under duality; VALUES must not be.
duality_audit.scope: the 9 UNREGISTERED families (0.3.0 addendum). Known-closed dualities are not re-reported.

affirmation_verb_finding.restated: the structural vocabulary is RETRACTION-ONLY (SCORES / DELEGATES_TO / SUPERSEDES / WITHDRAWS / RECANTS - three ways to take a claim back, zero to reaffirm), distinct from re-emit (=replacement) and from fresh_as_of (=alive, not endorsed).

per_family.consent:*: NO affirmation verb. A grant is producer-owned, so re-emitting an identical grant with a fresh asserted_at IS the affirmation and costs the producer nothing they should not be paying. What consent:* actually needs is fresh_as_of, so a consumer can tell 'still live' from 'never touched since 2024'.
per_family.capacity_assurance:*: NO - and adding one would be SYMMETRIZING AN AXIOM. CC 3.4.12 deliberately requires 'a fresh, attributable, independently-attested renewal on record' precisely so a steward cannot prolong control cheaply. A one-click 'reaffirm' verb is exactly the conservatorship-abuse affordance the clause forecloses.
per_family.ownership:*: NO verb, but YES to fresh_as_of - and this is the family where it is load-bearing: distinguishing 'owner alive but quiet' from 'owner provably dead' is the missing input to the unimplemented CC 3.2 no-permanent-ownerless-lock reclaim path.
per_family.trust:*: NO verb, YES to fresh_as_of. An untouched trust edge is today indistinguishable from an abandoned one, and CIRISEdge#386 leg B makes a live routing decision on that edge.
per_family.trace:*: NO. A trace is an existence record about a past event; reaffirming it is meaningless.
per_family.trace_summary:*: NO - it is a re-computable derived projection; recomputation is the affirmation.
per_family.config:*: NO - the version fold already gives last-write-wins semantics.

logical_gaps.why_a_defect: CC 3.2 states 'No permanent ownerless lock (MUST)' and points at CC 4.2.6 by analogy, but CC 2.4.1.1's four withdraws paths admit no third party against a LIVE incumbent, and CIRISPersist v21.4.0 contains zero seizure/reclaim/ownerless handling. A node whose owner dies is bricked for federation purposes with no wire path back.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: seed the deployment's WA/recovery key_id into subject_key_ids at owner-binding genesis so the EXISTING rule-2 direct-subject-revocation path admits a WA withdraws - closes a MUST with no new primitive.

logical_gaps.missing_dual: a delete visible to generic consumers
logical_gaps.why_a_defect: the dual exists twice in incompatible forms: an app-level ConfigValue::Null tombstone (visible only to config.rs-aware readers) and genuine withdraws/recants (visible fabric-wide). The default path is the invisible one, so a generic CEG consumer sees a live, unrevoked row for a deleted key.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: emit a structural withdraws against the prior attestation_id on every delete_config call, keeping the Null value as a read-optimisation only.

logical_gaps.missing_dual: narrowing an ALREADY-promoted row when the covering grant is withdrawn
logical_gaps.why_a_defect: CC 3.3.7 attaches a cessation obligation to an explicit retract/supersede, but no mechanism narrows or tombstones a row already stamped and served. Note the boundary: 'un-see' is impossible and MUST NOT be attempted (that would be symmetrizing the anti-rollback axiom); the missing dual is the enforceable CEASE, not a retroactive narrowing.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: on grant withdraw, emit a supersede that re-stamps cohort_scope narrower and require the serve gate to re-evaluate live grants per request rather than trusting the stamped value alone.

logical_gaps.why_a_defect: THE COMPOSITE DEFECT SHAPE. The fail-open-to-liberty axiom is enforced in ONE direction only: admission refuses an over-long window, but nothing flips a live binding non-live on wall-clock lapse. Restoration therefore depends on a reader consulting liveness - i.e. on someone looking - which is precisely what 'no action required of the recovered person' forbids.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: a reconcile sweep that marks lapsed bindings non-live and emits the hard_case:* audit row, independent of any read.

logical_gaps.why_a_defect: normalize_prefixes trims, dedupes and sorts, but never validates. A token that can never match any dimension ('scores:' - the attestation_type name) is accepted, hybrid-signed into a durable federation-tier governance object, and evaluated as a no-op at BOTH live enforcement points. Structurally identical to a carried-but-unprocessed field, except the field is the whole grant entry.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: reject or warn on any entry equal to a reserved wire-primitive name, and on any entry matching no known dimension family.

logical_gaps.why_a_defect: a derived, promotable projection with no rule tying its life to the raw trace_events rows it summarises. Tombstoning the source leaves a promoted summary standing - constitution-silent, and the summary carries the scorer-relevant features.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: make the derived row carry references_attestation_id to its source and fold source retraction into the projection.

logical_gaps.why_a_defect: integrity-only commitment with no fountain/degradable-plane retrieval, so CC 3.1.8.4's F-3 detector degrades to a bare existence hash for exactly the longest, highest-signal reasoning runs.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: either ship the retrieval path or make the manifest form explicitly non-admissible as detector input.

logical_gaps.missing_dual: external witness at genesis (it exists at recovery)
logical_gaps.why_a_defect: recovery requires an m-of-n pre-committed ceremony; genesis requires nothing but the root's own signature. The strong check guards the second event and not the first, and the self-loop is the degenerate 1-hop cycle CC 4.1.1 tells substrates to reject.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: require a co-attestation reference at charter genesis, or ratify an explicit CC 4.1 carve-out naming infra-charter self-loops.

logical_gaps.why_a_defect: witness_relation==self and cohort_scope==federation are enforced where the object is WRITTEN and never where it is READ. The CC 3.4.7 three-actor pattern exists because producer discipline is not a substrate guarantee: a forged grant from a hostile producer is admitted.
logical_gaps.minimal_fix: two admission checks in CIRISPersist, routed through the CC 4.5.1 amendment process (new enforcement surface, not a bugfix).

axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: capability required to RECEIVE; never required to send
axiomatic_asymmetries.cc_ref: CEG_REPLICATION_MODEL.md sec.1 + hash-pinned in tests/replication_policy_gate.rs (E3); CC 4.4.3.4.3 for the infra:serve credential
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: trace:* is the ONE family of 104 forbidden the default-public posture every other Attestation-riding family uses. Making serve symmetric with the rest 'for consistency' silently publishes sealed reasoning content.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: self-emission REQUIRED (trace:*, ownership:*, config:* proposed) vs FORBIDDEN (capacity:*, capacity_assurance:*)
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: opposite polarities on the same equality check
axiomatic_asymmetries.cc_ref: CC 3.4.5 vs CC 3.2 / persist admission.rs ('the inverse polarity of capacity:*'s anti-self rule')
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: a reviewer normalising both to one rule destroys either the anti-Goodhart floor (if self-emission is allowed everywhere) or the act of taking responsibility (if forbidden everywhere - nobody else can sign that you own your node).

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: absence of capacity_assurance resolves to CAPACITY; absence of age_assurance resolves to PROTECTION
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: two sibling ladders with deliberately OPPOSITE absence defaults
axiomatic_asymmetries.cc_ref: CC 3.4.12 ('Getting this backwards... would be catastrophic; it is forbidden') vs CC 3.4.11
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: 'harmonising' the two ladders' defaults would make every un-attested adult presumptively incapacitated. The constitution pre-emptively forbids exactly this edit.

axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: the steward must ACT to retain control; the ward need not act to regain it
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: requiring the ward to petition for restoration (the 'symmetric' design) is the documented conservatorship-abuse failure mode.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: the steward is excluded from the restoration denominator
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: one party has standing to bind and none to unbind
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: giving the steward a vote in ending their own authority is self-dealing by construction.

axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: ambiguity yields NO owner, never a picked winner
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: a deterministic lexicographic tie-break looks like robustness and is actually a silent laundering of contested ownership.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: trust is inbound, consent is outbound
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: the user may un-trust a root; the root cannot un-trust the user
axiomatic_asymmetries.cc_ref: CC 3.2 ('There is no single "trust the community" switch')
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: collapsing them makes 'attach a trust root' silently mean 'consent to replicate to it' - two independent axes fused into one switch.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: multi-subject consent revocation is OR, never quorum
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: any ONE subject's withdraws is terminal for ALL
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: quorum-softening is how a single person's revocation gets outvoted by co-subjects who benefit from the data staying up.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: a consent revocation may TRANSIT local tier but never REST there
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: retraction carries a tier obligation ordinary content does not
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: this is anti-rollback made operational: retraction must outrun assertion, so treating a revocation like any other row lets it sit un-promoted while the thing it revokes is already federated.
a 'helpful' widening to include derivative prefixes exports the denormalized scorer-input surface under a grant the operator wrote for raw traces.

axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: infra keys are CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY denied agency:*; agency keys are only denied infra:* by policy
axiomatic_asymmetries.cc_ref: CC 4.4.3.4.3 (cited as CC 1.13.5 in three repos - see the cross-reference-drift ask)
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: making the denial mutual and merely-policy-level removes the wire-checkable guarantee that a serving node cannot act.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: capacity misattestation is adjudicated, never slashed
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: routing a clinical misjudgement into slashing:* deters the witnesses the ladder depends on.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: protected non-transferable domains are WALLS, not gradients
axiomatic_asymmetries.direction: no attested band ever unlocks them
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: the whole point of an apophatic bound is that harm is enumerable and absolute while beneficence is a gradient; making the floor score-sensitive reintroduces the trade.

axiomatic_asymmetries.rule: the node signs config on the authenticated human's behalf
axiomatic_asymmetries.why_symmetrizing_would_break_it: NOT AN AXIOM. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for one: extra.updated_by is a plaintext string a compromised node process can set at will. Flagged as a trust-boundary weakness, not a preserved direction.

duality_audit.coverage_note: asymmetry_kind is populated for every 0.3.0 addendum row (families, matrix rows touched, standardization clusters). The 0.2.0 rows it does not touch are UNMARKED, and unmarked asymmetry is indistinguishable from a bug - back-filling them is the first task of 0.4.0.

freshness_floor.status: PROPOSED - does not exist on the wire today
freshness_floor.semantics: a signed temporal LOWER bound: 'this object was demonstrably alive no earlier than T'. Dual to the existing upper bounds (valid_until / expires_at / delegation_valid_until / deletion_window).

decomposition.merge: monotonic max - deterministic, total, anti-rollback, and therefore algebra-legal (a pure fold over two values).
decomposition.value_production: a signed touch-claim. now() is NOT pure, so producing the value is an ATTESTATION, never a transform opcode. This is why 'reading emits a claim' is CEG-native here rather than a special case.

freshness_floor.coalescing: round(precision) on the touch value so same-bucket touches dedupe on the wire
freshness_floor.privacy_row: touch-claims are cohort-scoped and consent-gated - an unrestricted read-receipt trail is an access-pattern surveillance surface, and for trace:* (already the one recipient-gated family) it would leak exactly who is reading whose reasoning.
freshness_floor.existing_gap: CIRISPersist has `last_seen_at`, but admission.rs:1795 states it is 'advisory liveness, not signed material'. fresh_as_of is its signed successor, not a duplicate.

demanded_by.why: HIGHEST VALUE. Distinguishing 'owner alive but quiet' from 'owner provably dead' is the missing input to CC 3.2's unimplemented no-permanent-ownerless-lock reclaim. An owner-binding whose owner has not signed anything in years is currently indistinguishable from a fresh one.
demanded_by.signer_form: self_touch, escalating to n_of_m_cosigned for a death finding

demanded_by.why: an untouched trust edge is indistinguishable from an abandoned one, and CIRISEdge#386 leg B makes a live routing decision on it. The charter especially: root-hood asserted once in 2025 and never touched should not read the same as a live root.

a standing replication grant with no expiry is currently 'live forever'. fresh_as_of lets a consumer distinguish a maintained grant from an abandoned one WITHOUT weakening the rule that only an explicit supersede/withdraw narrows it. Also gives the 24h promotion-SLA and deletion-SLA watchers a signed clock input rather than an advisory one.

ADMITTED WITH A GUARD. A freshness floor is useful for liveness of the ward's inalienable channel and the champion's key, but it MUST NOT be accepted anywhere the constitution requires 'a fresh, attributable, independently-attested renewal' - substituting a cheap touch for a renewal is exactly the axiom-symmetrising failure this audit is hunting.
demanded_by.signer_form: witness_touch only; NEVER self_touch by the steward

demanded_by.why: WEAK - corpus liveness only (is this node still serving the trace it advertised?). A per-trace floor is meaningless; a per-corpus floor may be useful to edge's advertise path.
NO - it is re-computable from source; recomputation timestamps are a projection concern, not a wire claim.
NO - the version fold already provides recency, and a touch trail on config reads is a surveillance surface with no consumer.

freshness_floor.asymmetry_note: monotonic-max is deliberately one-directional. A merge that could DECREASE the floor would let a stale replica resurrect a dead liveness claim - the same anti-rollback logic that makes tombstones project Global.

field_transforms.principle: STRICTLY TOTAL. Named opcodes, fixed arity, NO loops, NO recursion, NO user-defined functions. Composition is a finite DAG, so the registry row IS the termination witness.
field_transforms.rationale: a transform sits in the admission/serve path; a non-terminating one wedges the gate, and a Turing-complete dialect could express the very flows this system makes unrepresentable. Precedent: Bitcoin Script (no loops); EVM (only quasi-TC via gas); FHIRPath ('entirely declarative, no imperative aspects'); Confluent data contracts (non-TC CEL/JSONata).
separations: SEPARATE from version-migration rules - Confluent keeps data rules and migration rules distinct; fusing them yields an unauditable registry.

SEPARATE from heavy computation - the trace PII scrubber (NER+regex), the trace_summary extractor, RATCHET detectors and scorers are NOT opcodes. They are pinned by contract hash, not expressed in the algebra.
SEPARATE from access control - a transform changes what a field BECOMES on an egress path; it never decides WHETHER the row is served (that is cohort_scope/consent/capability).

opcodes.determinism_note: pure over a fixed edge list; edges are registry data, not code
pure; also the coalescing primitive for fresh_as_of
opcodes.precedent: differential-privacy coarsening; CIRISServer correlation.rs already coarsens lat/long

opcodes.determinism_note: pure; ALREADY IN the consent grammar as RestrictionOp::StripField
pure given the salt; salt provenance must be declared
pure (Pedersen or sha256 form); integrity-only, NOT an availability guarantee
opcodes.precedent: Pedersen commitments; trace_manifest content_hash is the sha256 form

opcodes.determinism_note: pure; one identity yields one nullifier per (epoch,scope), enabling double-emit detection without identity
randomised but verifiable; selective disclosure over a signed set
pure predicate - discloses the ANSWER, not the value

family_transform_rows.justification: SHIPPED and constitutionally grounded (CC 3.3.7 restriction grammar). The enforcement point is deliberately promotion, not serve - a stripped field never enters the signed federation-tier bytes.
family_transform_rows.asymmetry_note: strip at promotion is irreversible by design; there is no un-strip dual and there must not be.

family_transform_rows.justification: the shipped worked example in consent_grammar.rs; the family's semantics (sealed reasoning) justify redacting the highest-sensitivity leaf while preserving the trace skeleton.

the NER+regex scrubber is heavy computation with hard-fail-never-partial semantics. Declaring it as a registry transform would put an unbounded ML pass in the admission path. Pinned by module contract, kept out of the algebra deliberately.

family_transform_rows.egress_path: mint, when canonical bytes exceed the size cap
family_transform_rows.justification: the oversize path IS a commit opcode in all but name. Declaring it as such makes the integrity-only/availability-absent distinction machine-visible rather than a code comment.
family_transform_rows.asymmetry_note: commit has no retrieval dual today - see duality_audit.

family_transform_rows.justification: the extraction is heavy computation governed by TRACE_SUMMARY_EXTRACTION_SHA256. An unjustified transform here would be worse than none: the feature vector's whole value is being the faithful, contract-pinned reduction.

family_transform_rows.egress_path: serve to a downstream capability gate
family_transform_rows.transform: gte / in_range predicate - disclose the ANSWER ('is this domain currently incapacitated?') not the clinical band, level, or assessor identity
family_transform_rows.justification: the ONLY genuinely justified privacy transform in the addendum. A delegates_to admission gate needs a boolean; it does not need a clinical finding. CC 3.4.12's actor-access requirements (steward / champion / WA quorum) are about who may see the FULL row - the predicate form is what everyone else should get.
family_transform_rows.asymmetry_note: the predicate must never be invertible into the band; and it MUST NOT be offered for the protected non-transferable domains at all (those are walls, not queries).

family_transform_rows.justification: accountability is load-bearing: misattestation routes to moderation:capacity_misattestation, which requires an attributable attester. Anonymising the witness would make the adjudication dimension unenforceable.
the owner's signature IS the claim; redacting or deriving over it voids the object. A transform here is a category error.
the charter must be plaintext-legible ('the trust root cannot be an opaque blob'); the trust edge must be peer-visible for CIRISEdge#386 leg B to verify rooting.

family_transform_rows.transform: NONE - AND DO NOT ADD ONE
family_transform_rows.justification: the temptation is to redact auth.admin_key_ids on egress. That would be an unjustified transform papering over the actual defect: the row should never be federation-scoped in the first place. Fix cohort_scope, do not add a transform.

not_yet_justified: nullifier(epoch=voting_window, scope=contribution_id) for anonymous voting is the canonical worked example of a registry-declared transform, but its demander (vote:{contribution_id}) is a REGISTERED family outside this addendum's scope - noted so 0.4.0 picks it up rather than re-deriving it.
